nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that keeps a persistent reference to the input Buffer plus the validate and upgrade flags, and clears and reloads the tile from that buffer off the main thread.

nodes.name: AsyncSetData.Execute
nodes.summary: Rejects an empty buffer, clears the tile, and calls merge_from_compressed_buffer with the validate and upgrade flags, storing any exception as the worker error.

nodes.name: AsyncGetData
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that can zlib-compress the tile bytes on a worker thread and hands back a Buffer, which takes ownership of the internal tile string when release is set.

nodes.name: AsyncGetData.Execute
nodes.summary: When compression is requested, gzip-compresses the tile data into a new std::string with the chosen zlib level and strategy on the worker thread.

nodes.name: AsyncGetData.GetResult
nodes.summary: Returns an empty Buffer for an empty tile; otherwise an external Buffer that owns the compressed string or the released tile buffer (with a finalizer that adjusts V8 external memory), or a plain copy of the raw bytes.

nodes.name: AsyncAddData
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that pins the JS Buffer and merges its vector tile data, compressed or not, into the existing tile without clearing it first.

nodes.name: AsyncAddData.Execute
nodes.summary: Fails on a zero-length buffer and otherwise calls merge_from_compressed_buffer to append the decoded layers to the tile, with the validate and upgrade options.

nodes.name: setDataSync
nodes.summary: Synchronously replaces the tile data: it validates a non-empty Buffer and the validate/upgrade booleans, clears the tile, and loads the buffer with merge_from_compressed_buffer.

nodes.name: setData
nodes.summary: Async VectorTile.setData that delegates to setDataSync without a trailing callback, otherwise validates the Buffer and options and queues an AsyncSetData worker.

nodes.name: getDataSync
nodes.summary: Returns the tile protobuf as a Buffer: it parses compression ('gzip' or none), release, level (0 to 9), and strategy (FILTERED, HUFFMAN_ONLY, RLE, FIXED, DEFAULT), and then copies, releases, or zlib-compresses the bytes.

nodes.name: getData
nodes.summary: Async VectorTile.getData that falls back to getDataSync without a callback, parses the same compression, release, level, and strategy options, and queues an AsyncGetData worker.

nodes.name: addDataSync
nodes.summary: Synchronously merges an extra protobuf Buffer into the tile after it checks for a non-empty Buffer and boolean validate/upgrade options, and rethrows decode errors as JS exceptions.

nodes.name: addData
nodes.summary: Async VectorTile.addData that calls addDataSync when the last argument is not a function, else validates the Buffer and options and queues an AsyncAddData worker.

nodes.name: mapnik_vector_tile_image.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements VectorTile.addImage, addImageSync, addImageBuffer, and addImageBufferSync, which add a raster layer to the tile either from a mapnik.Image (re-encoded by a vector_tile_impl processor with an image format and scaling method) or from an encoded image Buffer.

nodes.name: addImageSync
nodes.summary: Validates a non-empty mapnik.Image, a layer name, and the image_scaling/image_format options (default bilinear and webp), wraps a copy of the image as a raster feature in a memory_datasource over the tile extent, and encodes it into the tile with a processor.

nodes.name: AsyncAddImage
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that holds the tile, an image_ptr, the layer name, the image format, and the scaling method, and builds and encodes the raster layer on a worker thread.

nodes.name: AsyncAddImage.Execute
nodes.summary: Copies the image into a mapnik::raster feature, pushes it into a memory_datasource with the tile extent, adds an EPSG:3857 layer to a temporary Map, and runs processor::update_tile on the worker thread.

nodes.name: addImage
nodes.summary: Async VectorTile.addImage that needs at least an Image and a layer name, delegates to addImageSync when the last argument is not a callback, validates the options, and queues an AsyncAddImage worker.

nodes.name: addImageBufferSync
nodes.summary: Synchronously adds an encoded image Buffer as a raster tile layer: it checks for a non-empty Buffer and a layer name string and calls add_image_buffer_as_tile_layer.

nodes.name: AsyncAddImageBuffer
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that keeps a persistent reference to the image Buffer with its data pointer and length, and adds it as a raster layer off the main thread.

nodes.name: AsyncAddImageBuffer.Execute
nodes.summary: Calls add_image_buffer_as_tile_layer with the pinned buffer bytes and the layer name, and records any exception as the worker error.

nodes.name: addImageBuffer
nodes.summary: Async VectorTile.addImageBuffer that falls back to addImageBufferSync with fewer than three arguments, validates the callback, Buffer, and layer name, and queues an AsyncAddImageBuffer worker.

nodes.name: mapnik_vector_tile_info.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the static VectorTile.info(buffer), a debug helper that reports per-layer feature counts, layer versions, and protobuf validity errors for a raw or gzip/zlib-compressed .mvt buffer.
nodes.languageNotes: The unsupported-version check compares the running tile `version` variable, not the `layer_version` of the current layer, so a bad version on the first layer is not flagged on that layer.

nodes.name: info
nodes.summary: Decompresses the buffer when needed, walks the tile LAYERS with protozero, counts point, linestring, polygon, unknown, and raster features with layer_is_valid, and returns {layers, errors, tile_errors} that flags repeated layer names, mixed versions, unknown tags, and invalid PBF data.

nodes.name: mapnik_vector_tile_json.cpp
nodes.summary: Converts vector tiles to and from JSON: toJSON decodes the raw protobuf layers, features, tags, and geometry; toGeoJSON/toGeoJSONSync reproject features to WGS84 and write GeoJSON FeatureCollections; addGeoJSON encodes an inline GeoJSON string as a new tile layer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses template visitors over the mapnik geometry variant (geometry_type_name, geometry_array_visitor) and over the protobuf attribute value variant (json_value_visitor). addGeoJSON reads area_threshold with Int32Value, so fractional thresholds are truncated.

nodes.name: geometry_type_name
nodes.summary: Geometry variant visitor that maps a mapnik geometry to its GeoJSON type name (Point, LineString, Polygon, the Multi* types, GeometryCollection, or Empty) for the decode_geometry output of toJSON.

nodes.name: geometry_array_visitor
nodes.summary: Recursive variant visitor that converts a decoded mapnik geometry (points, line strings, rings, polygons, multi geometries, collections) into nested Napi::Array coordinate arrays.

nodes.name: json_value_visitor
nodes.summary: Visitor that sets one decoded vector tile attribute value (string, bool, int64, uint64, double, or float) on a JS properties object under the given key name.

nodes.name: layer_to_geojson
nodes.summary: Reads every feature of one protobuf layer through tile_datasource_pbf with an unbounded query, reprojects each geometry from EPSG:3857 to EPSG:4326, and appends comma-separated GeoJSON feature strings to the result; it returns true when it wrote at least one feature.

nodes.name: write_geojson_array
nodes.summary: Writes a JSON array that holds one named FeatureCollection per tile layer, with layer_to_geojson for the features of each layer.

nodes.name: write_geojson_all
nodes.summary: Writes a single FeatureCollection that merges the features of all tile layers and skips layers that have no features.

nodes.name: write_geojson_layer_index
nodes.summary: Writes a named FeatureCollection for the layer at a zero-based index and returns false when the tile has no layer at that index.

nodes.name: write_geojson_layer_name
nodes.summary: Writes a FeatureCollection for the layer with the given name and returns false when the tile has no layer reader for that name.

nodes.name: AsyncToGeoJSON
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that builds the GeoJSON string for VectorTile.toGeoJSON on a worker thread for all layers, an array of layers, a named layer, or an indexed layer, as the geojson_write_type selects.

nodes.name: AsyncToGeoJSON.Execute
nodes.summary: Switches on the stored geojson_write_type and calls write_geojson_all, write_geojson_array, write_geojson_layer_name, or write_geojson_layer_index to fill the result string.

nodes.name: toJSON
nodes.summary: Decodes the tile protobuf into a JS array of layer objects with name, extent, version, and features; each feature gets id, type, properties from the key/value tables, optional raster bytes, and geometry as raw command integers or, with decode_geometry, as coordinate arrays plus geometry_type.

nodes.name: toGeoJSONSync
nodes.summary: Synchronous GeoJSON export that accepts '__all__', '__array__', a layer name, or a zero-based layer index, validates the index range, and returns the GeoJSON string.

nodes.name: toGeoJSON
nodes.summary: Async GeoJSON export that falls back to toGeoJSONSync without a callback, maps the layer argument to a geojson_write_type after it checks the name or index, and queues an AsyncToGeoJSON worker.

nodes.name: addGeoJSON
nodes.summary: Encodes a GeoJSON string as a new named layer: it builds a temporary EPSG:3857 Map with an inline geojson datasource layer in EPSG:4326 and runs a vector_tile_impl processor with the area_threshold, strictly_simple, simplify_distance, multi_polygon_union, fill_type, and process_all_rings options.

nodes.name: mapnik_vector_tile_render.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements VectorTile.render, which draws the tile layers with the style of a mapnik.Map onto a mapnik.Image (AGG), a CairoSurface (Cairo or native SVG output), or a Grid (UTF grid for one layer) on a worker thread, with optional z/x/y override, buffer, scale, and variables.
nodes.languageNotes: Holds the render target in a mapnik::util::variant<dummy_surface, Image*, CairoSurface*, Grid*> and uses ref/deref visitors to keep the JS object alive during the async job. In the Grid branch of render, a local `std::size_t layer_idx` shadows the outer variable, so the worker always gets layer index 0; also, OnWorkComplete calls Map::release() although render never calls acquire().

nodes.name: process_layers
nodes.summary: Template helper that, for each map layer that is visible at the scale denominator and present in the tile, copies the layer, sets the map SRS, attaches a tile_datasource_pbf for that layer, and calls apply_to_layer on the given AGG, Cairo, or SVG renderer.

nodes.name: AsyncRenderTile
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that holds the Map, the tile, the surface variant, variables, layer index, z/x/y, size, buffer, scale, and renderer flags, renders the tile, and releases the Map and surface references when done.

nodes.name: AsyncRenderTile.Execute
nodes.summary: Computes the Mercator bbox from the tile or the z/x/y override, builds a request and scale denominator, and renders with grid_renderer for a Grid, cairo_renderer or svg_renderer into the CairoSurface stream, or agg_renderer for an RGBA8 Image.

nodes.name: AsyncRenderTile.OnWorkComplete
nodes.summary: Releases the Map in-use flag, drops the Map reference, and unreferences the surface through deref_visitor before the worker completes.

nodes.name: AsyncRenderTile.GetResult
nodes.summary: Returns a new Image or Grid wrapper for raster targets, or flushes the CairoSurface stream and returns a new CairoSurface with the same format and size that carries the rendered data.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: VectorTile.render entry point that validates the Map, the surface, and the callback, parses z/x/y (all three together, below 2^z), buffer_size, scale, scale_denominator, variables, renderer ('cairo' or 'svg'), and grid layer/fields, then refs the surface and Map and queues AsyncRenderTile.

nodes.name: mapnik_vector_tile_simple_valid.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements VectorTile.reportGeometrySimplicity(Sync) and reportGeometryValidity(Sync), which check every tile feature with Boost.Geometry is_simple/is_valid and return the failing features with layer, feature id, message, and GeoJSON; the file compiles only when BOOST_VERSION >= 105800.
nodes.languageNotes: The whole translation unit is inside #if BOOST_VERSION >= 105800, so the tree-sitter extraction found no definitions; the function and class nodes of this file come from a manual read of the source.

nodes.name: layer_not_simple
nodes.summary: Queries all features of one protobuf layer through tile_datasource_pbf and records a not_simple_feature (layer name, feature id) for each geometry that fails mapnik::geometry::is_simple.

nodes.name: visitor_geom_valid
nodes.summary: Geometry variant visitor that runs mapnik::geometry::is_valid on points, lines, polygons, and multi geometries (part by part when split_multi_features is set) and records a not_valid_feature with the message, layer, id, and a one-feature GeoJSON FeatureCollection.

nodes.name: layer_not_valid
nodes.summary: Validates one layer through tile_datasource_pbf (reprojected to EPSG:4326 when lat_lon is set, in EPSG:3857 when web_merc is set) or, by default, by decoding raw tile-grid geometry from the protobuf features, and applies visitor_geom_valid to each feature.

nodes.name: vector_tile_not_simple
nodes.summary: Iterates over every LAYERS message in the tile protobuf and calls layer_not_simple with the tile x, y, and z to collect non-simple features.

nodes.name: make_not_simple_array
nodes.summary: Converts the collected not_simple_feature records into a JS array of {layer, featureId} objects.

nodes.name: vector_tile_not_valid
nodes.summary: Walks each layer of the tile protobuf and calls layer_not_valid with the split_multi_features, lat_lon, and web_merc flags to collect invalid features.

nodes.name: make_not_valid_array
nodes.summary: Builds a JS array of {layer, message, featureId, geojson} objects from the collected not_valid_feature records.

nodes.name: AsyncGeometrySimple
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that runs vector_tile_not_simple on a worker thread and returns the array of non-simple features to the reportGeometrySimplicity callback.

nodes.name: AsyncGeometrySimple.Execute
nodes.summary: Fills the result vector with vector_tile_not_simple on the worker thread and sets a worker error if the check throws.

nodes.name: AsyncGeometryValid
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that stores the split_multi_features, lat_lon, and web_merc flags, runs vector_tile_not_valid in the background, and returns the array of invalid features.

nodes.name: AsyncGeometryValid.Execute
nodes.summary: Calls vector_tile_not_valid with the stored flags on the worker thread and converts exceptions into the worker error.

nodes.name: reportGeometrySimplicitySync
nodes.summary: Synchronously collects the tile geometries that are not OGC simple and returns them as an array of {layer, featureId} objects.

nodes.name: reportGeometryValiditySync
nodes.summary: Parses the optional split_multi_features, lat_lon, and web_merc booleans and synchronously returns the array of OGC-invalid features with messages and GeoJSON.

nodes.name: reportGeometrySimplicity
nodes.summary: Async simplicity report that runs the sync version when it gets no arguments, otherwise requires a callback and queues an AsyncGeometrySimple worker.

nodes.name: reportGeometryValidity
nodes.summary: Async validity report that delegates to the sync version for zero arguments or one non-function argument, parses the options when present, and queues an AsyncGeometryValid worker.

nodes.name: object_to_container.hpp
nodes.summary: Header-only helper that copies the own properties of a JS object into a mapnik::attributes map; the render paths use it to pass the 'variables' option to Mapnik expressions and datasource queries.

nodes.name: object_to_container
nodes.summary: Copies boolean, string (UTF-8 transcoded to mapnik unicode), and numeric JS properties into mapnik::attributes, stores whole numbers that fit in Int32 as value_integer and other numbers as double, and skips other value types.

nodes.name: PGPool.js
nodes.summary: Defines PGPool, an LRU-cached wrapper around a pg Pool that coalesces concurrent identical SQL queries and caches each post-processed result (default 10000 entries, 4-minute expiry). Config uses it to cache the GeoJSON-filled Mapnik XML per tile query.
nodes.languageNotes: Request coalescing: the queue and isFetching maps keyed by SQL text let concurrent callers for one query share a single pool.query call. The lru-cache options use the older maxAge key.

nodes.name: PGPool
nodes.summary: Holds the injected pg Pool, an lru-cache keyed by SQL text, and a per-SQL callback queue, and exposes getQuery and hasCached so tile requests for the same query share one database round trip.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.summary: Queues the callback under its SQL string and runs pool.query only when no fetch for that SQL is in flight; on success it applies handleResult, drains the queue, and stores the result in the LRU cache, and on error it rejects every queued callback.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Returns a Promise for a SQL result that resolves from the LRU cache on a hit and otherwise delegates to fetch with the handleResult transformer, which Config uses to turn rows into Mapnik XML.

nodes.name: PGPool.spec.js
nodes.summary: Jest spec for PGPool that mocks pg's Pool to check LRU eviction and a 1-second expiry with cacheSize 1, and to check that queued getQuery calls for two SQL strings each resolve with their own mocked rows. Both cases build PGPool without the pool option that the constructor reads, so the mocked Pool never reaches the class.

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: Express app for the Greenstand tile server: it creates a pg Pool from DB_URL and PG_POOL_SIZE, builds a Config, registers Mapnik fonts and input plugins, and serves 256x256 PNG tiles and UTF grid JSON tiles at /:z/:x/:y and /new/:z/:x/:y. It also serves the static viewer under /viewer and a version banner for every other path.
nodes.languageNotes: Each handler wraps the callback-style node-mapnik render, encode, and fromString APIs in Promises; the /new routes duplicate the root handlers line for line.

nodes.name: buildMapInstance
nodes.summary: Creates a 256x256 mapnik.Map for tile x/y/z: it computes 100-pixel buffered lon/lat bounds with xyz_to_envelope_db_buffer, gets the Mapnik XML from Config.getXMLString, loads it with fromString, and sets map.extent to the Web Mercator envelope from xyz_to_envelope.

nodes.name: GET /:z/:x/:y.png
nodes.summary: Renders the requested tile through buildMapInstance into a 256x256 mapnik.Image, encodes it as PNG, and returns it with Content-Type image/png; any error returns HTTP 500 with a JSON message.

nodes.name: GET /:z/:x/:y.grid.json
nodes.summary: Renders layer l1 of the tile into a 256x256 mapnik.Grid with the fields id, latlon, count, and type (plus zoom_to at zoom 9 and below) and returns the UTF grid, encoded at resolution 4 with features, as JSON.

nodes.name: GET /new/:z/:x/:y.png
nodes.summary: PNG tile route under /new that adds newIcons: true to the query params before buildMapInstance; Config.getXMLString ignores that flag, so the icon choice still comes only from the icon query parameter.

nodes.name: GET /new/:z/:x/:y.grid.json
nodes.summary: UTF grid route under /new that passes newIcons: true into buildMapInstance and otherwise repeats the root grid handler, including the zoom_to field for zoom 9 and below.

nodes.name: ALL *
nodes.summary: Catch-all handler that answers every unmatched path with HTTP 200 and the text 'Welcome to Greenstand tile server, version:' followed by the package.json version.

nodes.name: config.js
nodes.summary: Builds the Mapnik XML style for each tile request: Config gets SQL from Map.js, then for zoom 1-15 fetches rows through PGPool and inlines them as GeoJSON, and for deeper zooms injects the SQL and DB_URL credentials into a PostGIS template. It also exports replace, config, and configFreetown, which rewrite greenstand/layers/postgis.xml with DB_URL credentials.
nodes.languageNotes: Template selection is a nested switch on json, tree, and icon. The zoomLevelInt > 15 branch inside the GeoJSON path never runs, because GeoJSON mode applies only to zoom 1-15, and the constructor's newIcons argument is unused.

nodes.name: replace
nodes.summary: Parses DB_URL (postgresql://user:password@host:port/db) and swaps the hard-coded postgres user, 172.17.0.2 host, 5432 port, greenstand password, and treetracker_dev database name in a Mapnik XML string for the real values.

nodes.name: config
nodes.summary: Reads greenstand/layers/postgis.xml, fills in the DB_URL credentials with replace, and writes the output to greenstand/layers/postgis.prod.xml.

nodes.name: configFreetown
nodes.summary: Like config, but it also swaps the trees table subquery for SQL that keeps active trees whose planters belong to the 'freetown' entity hierarchy (through getEntityRelationshipChildren), then writes greenstand/layers/postgis.freetown.prod.xml.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Holds the pg Pool and a PGPool cache sized by the CACHE_SIZE and CACHE_EXPIRE env vars, and exposes getXMLString to turn tile options (zoom, userid, wallet, timeline, map_name, bounds, icon) into a complete Mapnik XML document.

nodes.name: getXMLString
nodes.summary: Decides GeoJSON mode and bounds use, calls Map.init and Map.getQuery for the tile SQL, then either turns PGPool rows into an inline GeoJSON FeatureCollection (throwing above 5 MB) or substitutes the SQL into a credential-filled PostGIS template.

nodes.name: getXML
nodes.summary: Selects one of the xml.js or xml2.js template strings from the json, tree, and icon flags: 'ptk-b' picks the green xml2 variants, 'ptk-s' picks the small variants, and 'o' or no icon falls back to the original orange templates.

nodes.name: checkUseBounds
nodes.summary: Returns whether the tile SQL gets the bounding box: never above zoom 15, always for map_name org maps, never for wallet or userid maps, and otherwise only above MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_USING_GLOBAL_DATASET.

nodes.name: config.pg.test.js
nodes.summary: Integration Jest suite that needs a live PostGIS database at DB_URL: it runs the 'case1' cluster SQL and builds GeoJSON from the rows, and renders zoom 2 tile 1/1 to map.png from xml.js, from greenstand/stylesheet2.xml, and from getXMLString with a UTF grid. It imports getXMLString from config.js, which no longer exports that name, so the getXMLString cases call undefined.

nodes.name: config.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest suite with a mocked pg Pool that checks config() and configFreetown() substitute DB_URL credentials (and the getEntityRelationshipChildren query) into postgis XML, and expects getXMLString to pick SQL 'case1' to 'case4' by zoom, userid, wallet, and map_name. It reads the output from test/ instead of greenstand/layers/ and calls a getXMLString export that config.js no longer provides.

nodes.name: experimental.test.js
nodes.summary: Experimental Jest case without assertions that loads an inline Mapnik XML string, with a pin_29px.png PointSymbolizer over the GeoJSON file greenstand/trees_sample.geojson, through Map.fromString to check that the style parses.

nodes.name: font.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest cases that register the DejaVu fonts from test/data/map-a and map-b on a mapnik.Map, assert that 'DejaVu Serif Condensed Bold' and 'DejaVu Serif Condensed Bold Italic' are available, and render TextSymbolizer maps (one over trees_text.geojson) to PNG files under /tmp/test.

nodes.name: server.js
nodes.summary: Process entry point that loads .env through dotenv, sets loglevel to info, asserts with expect-runtime that MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_USING_GLOBAL_DATASET and MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET are defined, and starts the Express app from app.js on PORT.

nodes.name: sheet.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest suite that renders test/stylesheet.xml and test/postgis.xml with node-mapnik to PNG and UTF grid files under /tmp/test, checks the binding version (4.5.6, Mapnik 4.0.0), and calls the Express app with supertest on / and /0/0/0.png; it.only limits a run to the grid case.

nodes.name: sphericalmercator.js
nodes.summary: Exports a singleton SphericalMercator that converts between lon/lat, 256-pixel tile pixels, and Web Mercator envelopes for zoom levels 0-20 through a mapnik.Projection. It also gives a pixel-buffered lon/lat bbox, clipped to +/-85.0511 latitude, for the tile SQL queries.
nodes.languageNotes: Prototype-based class: the constructor fills lookup arrays and the methods live on SphericalMercator.prototype; module.exports is one shared instance.

nodes.name: SphericalMercator
nodes.summary: Constructor that precomputes the per-zoom pixel scale tables (Bc, Cc, zc, Ac) for 21 zoom levels at a 256-pixel tile size and stores the Web Mercator proj4 string.

nodes.name: xyz_to_envelope
nodes.summary: Converts tile x/y/zoom (optionally TMS-flipped) to a lon/lat box through px_to_ll and projects it to a Web Mercator envelope with mapnik.Projection.forward; app.js uses the result as the map extent.

nodes.name: xyz_to_envelope_db_buffer
nodes.summary: Expands the tile pixel corners by a pixel buffer, converts them to lon/lat, and clips them to valid longitude and Web Mercator latitude ranges, which gives the WGS84 bounds that Config passes into the tree SQL.

nodes.name: sphericalmercator.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest spec that checks xyz_to_envelope_db_buffer with a 100-pixel buffer at zoom 2 for tiles 2/1, 1/0, and 1/3 against ST_MakeEnvelope bounds captured from real SQL logs.

nodes.name: xml.js
nodes.summary: Exports the original orange-icon Mapnik XML templates: xml (PostGIS cluster layer with cluster_46px and cluster_63px shields), xmlTree (PostGIS tree layer with pin_29px.png), and xmlJson and xmlJsonForTree, which use an inline GeoJSON datasource with a json_data placeholder.
nodes.languageNotes: The templates carry placeholder DB credentials (postgres, 172.17.0.2, greenstand, treetracker_dev) and the literal 'select * from trees', which config.js swaps out at runtime with string replace.

nodes.name: xml2.js
nodes.summary: Exports the green 'ptk' icon variants of the Mapnik XML templates: xml2 and xmlTree2 (PostGIS layers with original_size_shadowless.png shields and tree_new.png points), xmlJson2 and xmlJsonForTree2 (inline GeoJSON with Lato Regular labels and tree_icon.png), and xmlJson3 and xmlTree3, derived by regex replace.
nodes.languageNotes: xmlJson3 shrinks xmlJson2 through chained regex replaces (scale 0.81, shield-dy -2, size 12). The xmlTree3 regex targets scale(0.33), which xmlTree2 does not contain, so xmlTree3 is identical to xmlTree2.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: CommonJS barrel that re-exports the node-mapnik binding module from lib/mapnik.js unchanged.

nodes.name: mapnik.js
nodes.summary: Upstream node-mapnik loader and package main: it finds the native binding with @mapbox/node-pre-gyp, applies env vars from mapnik_settings.js, defaults VRT_SHARED_SOURCE to 0, and adds version plus font and plugin registration helpers. It also registers MAPNIK_FONT_PATH fonts and adds typeName, toWKB, and toWKT prototype helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: The JavaScript layer monkey-patches prototypes of the native mapnik.Geometry and mapnik.Feature classes after the binding loads.

nodes.name: getGeometryType
nodes.summary: Maps a numeric mapnik.Geometry type constant to its name (Point, LineString, Polygon, the Multi* types, or GeometryCollection), with 'Unknown' as the fallback; Geometry.prototype.typeName uses it.

nodes.name: register_default_fonts
nodes.summary: Registers the bundled font directory from settings.paths.fonts recursively with mapnik.register_fonts, when the binary package ships one.

nodes.name: register_default_input_plugins
nodes.summary: Registers the bundled datasource input plugins from settings.paths.input_plugins with mapnik.register_datasources, which the PostGIS and GeoJSON layers of the tile server need.

nodes.name: register_system_fonts
nodes.summary: Registers OS font directories (/usr/share/fonts and ~/.fonts on Linux, BSD, and SunOS; /Library/Fonts on macOS; C:\Windows\Fonts on Windows) and returns true only when the font count grows.

nodes.name: Map.js
nodes.summary: Defines the Map class that the tile server uses to pick a SQL builder from greenstand/sqls by map mode (single tree, user, wallet, organization map_name, timeline, or default) and zoom level, then runs the query on a pg pool to fetch tree points or clusters.
nodes.languageNotes: CommonJS module (module.exports) with async/await. SQLCase1 and SQLZoomTargetCase1V2 are required but never instantiated, and the user and wallet count queries interpolate request values straight into the SQL text instead of bind parameters.

nodes.name: Map
nodes.summary: Holds a pg pool and the active SQL builder: init(settings) selects the builder, getQuery and getZoomTargetQuery expose its SQL, and getPoints and getZoomTargets run it on the pool.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: Reads treeid, zoom_level, userid, wallet, map_name, timeline, and bounds from settings, counts trees for user or wallet maps, and assigns this.sql to SQLCase2, SQLCase2Wallet, SQLCase2Timeline, SQLCase3, SQLCase3Timeline, SQLCase1Timeline, SQLCase1WithZoomTarget, or SQLCase4 by mode, zoom band (>15, 12-15, lower), and a 2000-tree threshold. The capture_id branch never runs because init does not set this.capture_id, and flavor and token are stored but not applied.

nodes.name: getPoints
nodes.summary: Gets the SQL from the selected builder, runs it on the pg pool, logs the elapsed milliseconds and the first two rows, and returns the result rows for tile rendering.

nodes.name: getZoomTargets
nodes.summary: Runs the zoom target query on the pg pool when getZoomTargetQuery returns one and returns its rows; because init never sets sqlZoomTarget, it currently returns undefined.

nodes.name: Map.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest suite for Map that mocks pg Pool.prototype.query and checks which SQL case (case1 to case4, case6 zoom target) init selects for normal, user, single tree, wallet, token, flavor, and org map_name settings across zoom levels. Many expectations ({text, values} results, case6 zoom targets, token and flavor filters) do not match the current Map.js output.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses jest.mock('pg') and replaces Pool.prototype.query, but constructs Map without a pool, so the user-map count query in init has no pool to call.

nodes.name: SQLCase1.js
nodes.summary: Base SQL builder (case1) that aggregates tree counts per region from the active_tree_region table at a given zoom level, with optional planter, wallet, organization map_name, tree id, and bounding box filters, and returns cluster rows with K-formatted count_text labels.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds SQL with template literals and string concatenation of filter values (userId, wallet, mapName, bounds) rather than bind parameters.

nodes.name: SQLCase1
nodes.summary: Stateful builder whose setters (addFilterByUserId, addFilterByWallet, addMapNameFilter, setZoomLevel, setBounds) store criteria that getQuery assembles into a region-cluster SELECT over active_tree_region; getZoomLevel throws when no zoom level is set.

nodes.name: getJoin
nodes.summary: Returns case1 JOIN clauses: tree_region to trees for user or wallet filters, tree_region to the org_tree_id CTE for a map_name, and trees to wallet.token and wallet.wallet for a wallet.

nodes.name: getFilter
nodes.summary: Returns case1 AND clauses that filter by planter_id, by a tree_region.tree_id IN list built from treeIds, and by wallet.wallet.name.

nodes.name: getWith
nodes.summary: Returns a placeholder WITH clause, or for a map_name a recursive organization_children CTE over entity_relationship plus an org_tree_id CTE of trees from planters in up to 20 child organizations or from the planting organization.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Assembles the case1 SELECT on active_tree_region grouped by region_id, centroid, and type_id with count and count_text; at zoom level 2 it clamps centroid longitude to 170, and options.disableWith omits the WITH clause.

nodes.name: SQLCase1Timeline.js
nodes.summary: Extends SQLCase1 to restrict region cluster counts to trees whose time_created falls inside a 'YYYY-MM-DD_YYYY-MM-DD' timeline, replacing the parent joins with a single join from tree_region to trees.

nodes.name: SQLCase1Timeline
nodes.summary: SQLCase1 subclass with a static checkTimeline regex validator and an addTimeline setter; it overrides getJoin and getFilter to filter region counts by trees.time_created.

nodes.name: getFilter
nodes.summary: Splits the stored timeline on '_' into begin and end dates and returns an AND trees.time_created range clause that limits case1 region counts to that period.

nodes.name: SQLCase1Timeline.test.js
nodes.summary: Minimal Jest test that calls SQLCase1Timeline.checkTimeline with the valid range '2015-01-21_2016-12-31' and expects it not to throw.

nodes.name: SQLCase1V2.js
nodes.summary: Variant of SQLCase1 that filters organization trees for a map_name with an inline INNER JOIN derived table on tree_region.tree_id instead of a join to the org_tree_id CTE; Map.js does not import it.

nodes.name: SQLCase1V2
nodes.summary: SQLCase1 subclass that overrides getJoin to join tree_region to a derived table of organization tree ids for the stored mapName and redefines addMapNameFilter.

nodes.name: getJoin
nodes.summary: Returns a trees join for user filters and, for a map_name, an INNER JOIN to a tree_ids derived table of organization planter trees and planting_organization trees, matched on tree_region.tree_id.

nodes.name: SQLCase1WithZoomTarget.js
nodes.summary: Extends SQLCase1 so that, at zoom levels up to MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET, each region cluster also gets a zoom_to centroid of its most populated subregion two zoom levels deeper; above that level it falls back to the plain case1 query.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads process.env.MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET at query time; if the variable is unset, parseInt returns NaN and the comparison is always false.

nodes.name: SQLCase1WithZoomTarget
nodes.summary: SQLCase1 subclass whose only override, getQuery, wraps the parent cluster query as cluster_1 and LEFT JOINs a zoom_target subquery to fill the zoom_to column.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: When the zoom level is at or below MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET, nests the parent case1 query (without WITH) and joins, per region, the GeoJSON centroid of the most populated subregion at zoom+2 as zoom_to; otherwise returns the parent query unchanged.

nodes.name: SQLCase2.js
nodes.summary: Base SQL builder (case2) for high zoom levels that selects individual active trees as point rows from the trees table, with optional tree id, uuid, planter, wallet, flavor, certificate token, organization map_name, and bounding box filters.

nodes.name: SQLCase2
nodes.summary: Point query builder with setters for tree id, uuid, planter, wallet, flavor, token, map_name, and bounds; addTreesFilter throws 'dedicated', and getQuery logs and returns the SQL string.

nodes.name: getFilter
nodes.summary: Returns case2 AND clauses that match trees.id, trees.uuid, trees.planter_id, or wallet.wallet.name, and for a map_name keeps trees whose planter is in planter_in_org or whose planting organization has that map_name.

nodes.name: getJoinCriteria
nodes.summary: Returns extra case2 criteria: an app_flavor key and value check on tree_attributes, or an INNER JOIN to certificates by token; getQuery appends this text after the WHERE conditions.

nodes.name: getJoin
nodes.summary: Returns case2 INNER JOINs from trees to wallet.token and wallet.wallet for a wallet filter and to tree_attributes for a flavor filter.

nodes.name: getWith
nodes.summary: Returns a placeholder WITH clause, or for a map_name a recursive organization_children CTE and a planter_in_org CTE of planters that belong to up to 20 child organizations.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Builds and logs the case2 SELECT of active trees with geometry, GeoJSON latlon, id, lat, lon, and count 1, applying the WITH clause, joins, bounding box, filters, and join criteria, ordered by id descending.

nodes.name: SQLCase2Timeline.js
nodes.summary: Extends SQLCase2 to select active tree points inside a bounding box whose time_created falls in a timeline range, and returns a pg {text, values} query object instead of a plain SQL string.

nodes.name: SQLCase2Timeline
nodes.summary: SQLCase2 subclass that adds addTimeline, replaces getFilter with a time_created range, returns an empty getJoin, redefines the bounds methods, and returns a {text, values} object from getQuery.

nodes.name: getFilter
nodes.summary: Returns an AND trees.time_created range clause from the begin and end dates of the stored timeline, so case2 point rows only include trees created in that period; it does not validate the timeline format.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Builds and logs a case2 point SELECT of trees.id, lat, and lon for active trees in the bounding box and timeline range, and wraps the SQL in a pg {text, values: []} object.

nodes.name: SQLCase2Wallet.js
nodes.summary: Extends SQLCase2 for wallet maps: it selects active tree points joined to wallet.token on capture_id, keeps only tokens in the named wallet, and throws 'dedicated' for the user, flavor, token, and map_name filters.

nodes.name: SQLCase2Wallet
nodes.summary: SQLCase2 subclass that disables non-wallet filter setters by throwing, returns empty filter, join, and join criteria fragments and a placeholder WITH, and builds a wallet-scoped point query in getQuery.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Builds and logs a SELECT of active tree points joined to wallet.token by capture_id and lower(trees.uuid), wrapped as tree_token and joined to wallet.wallet to keep rows of the named wallet only.

nodes.name: SQLCase3.js
nodes.summary: SQL builder (case3) that clusters active trees on the fly with PostGIS ST_ClusterWithin, using a zoom-dependent cluster radius, and supports planter, wallet, flavor, certificate token, organization map_name, and bounding box filters.
nodes.languageNotes: The header comment notes that clustering the raw trees table directly is slow for large data sets, which is why Map.js only uses case3 for smaller user and wallet maps and mid zoom levels.

nodes.name: SQLCase3
nodes.summary: Cluster query builder with zoom, planter, wallet, flavor, token, map_name, and bounds setters plus getClusterRadius; its getQuery emits an ST_ClusterWithin SELECT with centroid, count, and count_text columns.

nodes.name: getClusterRadius
nodes.summary: Maps zoom levels 1 to 19 to an ST_ClusterWithin radius in degrees, from 10 at zoom 1 down to 0.003 at zoom 16 and 0 at zoom 17 and above.

nodes.name: getFilter
nodes.summary: Returns case3 AND clauses that match trees.planter_id for user maps and wallet.wallet.name for wallet maps before clustering.

nodes.name: getWith
nodes.summary: Builds the case3 WITH clause: a placeholder by default, or for a map_name the recursive organization_children CTE and an org_tree_id CTE that getJoin then joins to trees.id.

nodes.name: getJoin
nodes.summary: Returns case3 INNER JOINs from trees to the wallet tables, to tree_attributes for a flavor, to certificates for a token, and to org_tree_id for a map_name.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Logs 'Calculating clusters directly' and builds the case3 SELECT that unnests ST_ClusterWithin over filtered active trees and returns each cluster centroid as geometry and GeoJSON with count and count_text.

nodes.name: SQLCase3Timeline.js
nodes.summary: Extends SQLCase3 to cluster only trees whose time_created falls in a validated timeline range and drops all parent joins; it also keeps an unused getQuery2 variant of the cluster query.

nodes.name: SQLCase3Timeline
nodes.summary: SQLCase3 subclass with static checkTimeline validation, addTimeline, an empty getJoin, a time_created getFilter, and a legacy getQuery2; it inherits getQuery from SQLCase3.

nodes.name: getJoin
nodes.summary: Overrides the SQLCase3 join builder to return an empty string, so timeline cluster queries read the trees table without wallet, flavor, token, or organization joins.

nodes.name: getFilter
nodes.summary: Replaces the SQLCase3 planter and wallet filters with a trees.time_created range clause built from the timeline, so ST_ClusterWithin only clusters trees created in that period.

nodes.name: getQuery2
nodes.summary: Alternative case3 timeline query that returns only type, GeoJSON centroid, and count per ST_ClusterWithin cluster; no code in this batch calls it, so the inherited SQLCase3.getQuery runs instead.

nodes.name: SQLCase4.js
nodes.summary: SQL builder (case4) that reads precomputed clusters at zoom_level 14 from the clusters table, optionally limited to a bounding box, and formats count_text labels; Map.js uses it for default maps at zoom 12 to 15.

nodes.name: SQLCase4
nodes.summary: Small builder with setBounds, a getBoundingBoxQuery on the location column, and a getQuery that selects from the precomputed clusters table at zoom level 14.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Returns the case4 SELECT of id, location geometry, GeoJSON centroid and latlon, count, and count_text from the clusters table at zoom_level 14 within the optional bounding box.

nodes.name: SQLZoomTargetCase1.js
nodes.summary: Zoom target query builder (case6) that, for each populated region at a zoom level, finds the most populated subregion two levels deeper and returns its centroid, with optional tree id and bounding box filters, as a parameterized {text, values} query.

nodes.name: SQLZoomTargetCase1
nodes.summary: Zoom target builder that stores tree ids, zoom level, and bounds; getZoomLevel throws 'zoom level required' when unset, and getQuery binds zoom and zoom+2 as $1 and $2.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Returns a {text, values} query that uses DISTINCT ON region.id to pick, per populated region, the subregion at zoom+2 with the highest tree total whose centroid lies inside it, filtered by tree ids and region centroid bounds.

nodes.name: SQLZoomTargetCase1V2.js
nodes.summary: Extends SQLZoomTargetCase1 to select organization trees for a map_name through the getEntityRelationshipChildren database function instead of an explicit tree id list; setTreeIds and addTreesFilter throw 'dedicated'.

nodes.name: SQLZoomTargetCase1V2
nodes.summary: SQLZoomTargetCase1 subclass that adds addMapNameFilter, overrides getFilter with an organization tree id subquery, and blocks setTreeIds and addTreesFilter by throwing.

nodes.name: getFilter
nodes.summary: For a map_name, returns an AND active_tree_region.tree_id IN clause over trees of planters in getEntityRelationshipChildren organizations and trees planted by the organization; the planter branch appears twice under UNION ALL.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context ignore list with a single entry, node_modules, so the Dockerfile's `COPY . ./` does not ship host dependencies into the image; `make release_base` reinstalls them inside the container with `npm install --ignore-scripts --clang`.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage image build for the Greenstand tile server: it copies the repo into /app, installs build-essential, zlib1g-dev, ca-certificates and a Node.js 14.21.3 tarball, compiles the node-mapnik native binding with `make release_base`, and runs `npm start`, which launches greenstand/server.js.
nodes.languageNotes: Every RUN uses sudo, so the base image runs as a non-root user with sudo rights. Lines 6 and 8 call `apt install` without `-y`; in a non-interactive build that works only when the packages are already present, because a confirmation prompt aborts the step. A TODO on line 9 proposes a rebuild from a Node 14 Alpine image.

nodes.name: tile-server-base
nodes.summary: The one build stage, based on the prebuilt greenstand/tile-server-base:first image; that base image must supply the Mapnik libraries and the mapnik-config tool that `make release_base` checks for, because this Dockerfile installs no Mapnik packages itself.

nodes.name: build-deploy.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that runs on pushes to master and next: it cuts a release with semantic-release, then builds the root Dockerfile with Buildx and pushes greenstand/treetracker-map-tile-server to DockerHub, tagged with the package.json version. A second job sets that tag in deployment/base with kustomize and applies the deployment/overlays/development build to the tile-server namespace on the DigitalOcean cluster named by DEV_CLUSTER_NAME.
nodes.languageNotes: The deploy job gets the image tag from the build job through an uploaded artifact file (image-tag-<sha>) instead of job outputs, and it sets a step output with the deprecated ::set-output command. The Bash brace expansion @semantic-release/{git,exec,changelog} installs three plugins in one npm command.

nodes.name: deploy-dev-next.yml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched workflow that checks out a given git-tag, reads the package.json version, and runs kustomize on deployment-next/base and deployment-next/overlays/development to apply that image to the tile-server-next namespace on the DEV_CLUSTER_NAME cluster. The deployment-next/ directory that it uses is not present in this repo.

nodes.name: deploy-dev.yml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched workflow that redeploys a chosen git-tag to development: it sets greenstand/treetracker-map-tile-server:<package.json version> as the image in deployment/base and applies the deployment/overlays/development kustomize build to the tile-server namespace. It saves the kubeconfig of the cluster in the TEST_CLUSTER_NAME secret, not DEV_CLUSTER_NAME.

nodes.name: deploy-prod.yml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched workflow that promotes a chosen git tag to production: it checks out the tag with actions/checkout@v4, sets the package.json version as the image in deployment/base, and applies the deployment/overlays/production kustomize build to the tile-server namespace. It authenticates with the DIGITALOCEAN_PRODUCTION_TOKEN secret on the cluster named by PRODUCTION_CLUSTER_NAME.

nodes.name: deploy-test.yml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched workflow that deploys a chosen git tag to the test environment: it sets the package.json version as the image in deployment/base and applies the deployment/overlays/test kustomize build to the tile-server namespace. It uses the DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN secret and the DigitalOcean cluster named by TEST_CLUSTER_NAME.
nodes.languageNotes: The workflow runs `kustomize edit set image` in deployment/base and then builds the overlay. The overlay gets the new image tag through its `bases: ../../base` reference.

nodes.name: .env
nodes.summary: Local dotenv settings for the Greenstand tile server: PORT=23300, CACHE_SIZE=10000 and CACHE_EXPIRE=60 for the query cache, PG_POOL_SIZE=60, and a value of 6 for both MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_USING_GLOBAL_DATASET and MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET. It also sets NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED='0'.
nodes.languageNotes: NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED='0' turns off TLS certificate verification for every outbound TLS connection of the Node process, not only the PostgreSQL connection.

nodes.name: .prettierrc.json
nodes.summary: Prettier rules for the repo's JavaScript: semicolons on, trailing commas set to "all", and single quotes. The prettier, eslint-plugin-prettier, and eslint-config-prettier devDependencies in package.json apply these rules.

nodes.name: .travis.yml
nodes.summary: Legacy upstream node-mapnik Travis CI matrix on Node 12: Linux and macOS (xcode11) release and debug builds through make, plus ASan, g++-6, SSE_MATH=false, clang-format, clang-tidy, and coverage jobs. Most jobs start a local PostGIS with scripts/postgis/setup_and_run.sh, run npm test, and can publish binaries with scripts/publish.sh.
nodes.languageNotes: Tests run in before_script instead of script so that the first failing command stops the job; matrix entries override the global install and before_script keys to change toolchains or skip publishing.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: Release history whose top part is Greenstand semantic-release entries from 4.6.0 (2021) to 4.36.7 (2026-09-29): PostGIS tile rendering, PGPool caching, SQL tuning for org and wallet maps, tree and cluster icons, and Kubernetes deployment fixes. Below the '# Changelog' heading it keeps the upstream node-mapnik history from 4.5.6 back to 0.1.0 (2011).

nodes.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
nodes.summary: Upstream node-mapnik contributor guide that requires 100% line test coverage (LCOV_EXCL markers for unreachable code) and explains local docs builds with npm run docs. It describes the release flow: Mapnik SDK updates, '[publish binary]' commits, mapnik-swoop downstream tests, git tags, make testpack, and npm publish.

nodes.name: LICENSE.txt
nodes.summary: BSD 3-clause license text, copyright 2010-2012 Dane Springmeyer, inherited from upstream node-mapnik; package.json declares the matching BSD-3-Clause license.

nodes.name: Makefile
nodes.summary: Build entry point for the native mapnik addon: release and debug fetch the mason Mapnik SDK through scripts/install_deps.sh, then release_base and debug_base check mapnik-config and run node-pre-gyp configure build with SSE_MATH and the glibc workaround (the Dockerfile runs make release_base). Other targets run the coverage, clang-tidy, clang-format, and sanitizer scripts, clean and distclean, Xcode scheme generation, docs, npm test, and an npm pack check (testpack).
nodes.languageNotes: release calls release_base through a recursive $(MAKE) with mason_packages/.link/bin on PATH and -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0; file targets such as ./node_modules/.bin/node-pre-gyp act as install-once prerequisites.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project README titled treetracker-tile-server (previously node-mapnik-1) that still carries upstream node-mapnik content: JavaScript examples that render a stylesheet to PNG, convert JPEG to PNG, and convert a shapefile to GeoJSON, plus platform requirements, binary install notes, and source builds with make release, make debug, or make release_base against mapnik-config. It does not describe the Greenstand Express tile server under greenstand/.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Static landing page from upstream node-mapnik (Node Mapnik 3.5.0) with npm install instructions, the README example that renders test/stylesheet.xml to map.png, and links to the 3.5 and 3.4 API reference. It loads highlight.js and the GitHub buttons script from CDNs, and no active code in the repo serves it.

nodes.name: map.json
nodes.summary: Stray 15-byte file whose only content is the string '[object Object]', which is what a JavaScript object becomes when it is written to a file without JSON.stringify. It is not valid JSON and no code reads it.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for treetracker-map-tile-server 4.36.7: main is ./lib/mapnik.js, start and start-dev run greenstand/server.js with --max-old-space-size=1024 (node or nodemon), and install fetches or builds the native binding through node-pre-gyp from the binary block. It pins mapnik_version c3eda40e0, lists express, cors, dotenv, lru-cache, loglevel, and node-addon-api as dependencies, and keeps tape, jest, supertest, pg, knex, eslint, prettier, husky, and commitlint for development.
nodes.languageNotes: @mapbox/node-pre-gyp reads the binary block (module_name, module_path, host, remote_path, package_name) to find the prebuilt mapnik.node tarball. pg is a devDependency although greenstand/app.js requires it at runtime.

nodes.name: vcbuild.bat
nodes.summary: Windows helper from upstream node-mapnik that prints the Node version and arch, points PROJ_LIB, GDAL_DATA, and PATH at a local C:\code\mapnik-deps Mapnik SDK, deletes lib\binding, and runs node-pre-gyp build with --msvs_version=2013.
nodes.languageNotes: Batch file with no :LABEL subroutines; its hard-coded SDK paths make it a local developer script, and CHANGELOG 3.7.0 records that upstream removed Windows support.

nodes.name: database-connection-sealed-secret.yaml
nodes.summary: Bitnami SealedSecret template named database-connection with one encrypted key, db, whose base value is PLACEHOLDER. Each environment overlay patches in the real encrypted PostgreSQL connection string, which the Deployment injects as DB_URL.
nodes.languageNotes: A SealedSecret is encrypted with the public key of the cluster's sealed-secrets controller, so it is safe to commit to git. The controller decrypts it into a normal Secret inside the cluster.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Deployment that runs one replica of the greenstand/treetracker-map-tile-server image (tag VERSION, which CI replaces through kustomize) on the DigitalOcean microservices-node-pool, with soft pod anti-affinity across hosts. It sets PORT=3000, PG_POOL_SIZE=20, CACHE_SIZE, CACHE_EXPIRE, the two MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL thresholds (6), NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, and DB_URL from the database-connection secret.
nodes.languageNotes: containerPort 80 is informational only: the Node process listens on PORT 3000, and service.yaml targets port 3000. NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 turns off TLS certificate verification for every outbound TLS connection of the process, including the PostgreSQL connection.

nodes.name: kustomization.yaml
nodes.summary: Kustomize base that puts the tile server into the tile-server namespace and bundles deployment.yaml, mapping.yaml, service.yaml, and the database-connection SealedSecret. The CI workflows set the image tag in this directory, and the beta, development, production, and test overlays patch it; namespace.yaml is not in its resources list.

nodes.name: mapping.yaml
nodes.summary: Ambassador (getambassador.io/v2) Mapping that routes requests with the /tiles/ URL prefix to the treetracker-tile-server Service. It rewrites the prefix to / and allows 60000 ms per request, so slow tile renders do not time out at the gateway.

nodes.name: namespace.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Namespace manifest that declares the tile-server namespace, which the base kustomization and the kubectl apply commands of the deploy workflows target. The base kustomization does not include it, so the namespace must already exist in the cluster.

nodes.name: service.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Service named treetracker-tile-server (default ClusterIP type) that selects pods with the label app=treetracker-tile-server. It forwards TCP port 80, named http, to container port 3000, where the Express tile server listens.

nodes.name: database-connection-sealed-secret.yaml
nodes.summary: Bitnami SealedSecret patch for the beta overlay that replaces the base PLACEHOLDER with the encrypted `db` value of the `database-connection` secret. The sealed-secrets controller decrypts it into the PostGIS connection string that the beta Deployment injects as DB_URL.
nodes.languageNotes: A SealedSecret holds data encrypted with the cluster controller's public key, so the ciphertext can be committed to git; only the controller in the target cluster can decrypt it into a normal Secret.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Strategic-merge patch for the beta `treetracker-tile-server` Deployment that pins the image to greenstand/treetracker-map-tile-server:4.36.7 with 1 replica. It sets PORT 3000, PG_POOL_SIZE 20, CACHE_SIZE 10000, CACHE_EXPIRE 60000, MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_USING_GLOBAL_DATASET 15 (base is 6), MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET 6, and DB_URL from the `database-connection` secret.
nodes.languageNotes: In a strategic-merge patch, the containers list merges by container name, so fields this patch omits (base node affinity, pod anti-affinity, containerPort) stay from the base Deployment.

nodes.name: kustomization.yaml
nodes.summary: Kustomize entry point for the beta environment that builds on ../../base, moves all resources into the `tile-server-beta` namespace, and applies the beta sealed-secret, Deployment, and Ambassador Mapping patches. The namespace.yaml patch is commented out, and no GitHub Actions workflow in the repo builds this overlay.
nodes.languageNotes: This overlay references the base through `resources:`, while the production overlay uses the older `bases:` field; both resolve to the same base in kustomize.

nodes.name: mapping.yaml
nodes.summary: Ambassador Mapping patch that exposes the beta tile server under the `/tiles-next/` prefix (base uses `/tiles/`) and rewrites it to `/`. It allows CORS GET requests with Content-Type and Authorization headers from the origin https://prod-k8s.treetracker.org.

nodes.name: namespace.yaml
nodes.summary: Kubernetes Namespace manifest that declares the `tile-server-beta` namespace for the beta tile server. The beta kustomization.yaml has this file commented out, so `kustomize build` does not emit it and the namespace must already exist.

nodes.name: database-connection-sealed-secret.yaml
nodes.summary: Bitnami SealedSecret patch for the development cluster that replaces the base PLACEHOLDER with the real encrypted `db` value of the `database-connection` secret in the `tile-server` namespace. The tile-server Deployment reads this key as its DB_URL PostGIS connection string.
nodes.languageNotes: A SealedSecret holds data encrypted with the cluster controller's public key, so the ciphertext can be committed to git; only the in-cluster sealed-secrets controller can decrypt it into a normal Secret.

nodes.name: kustomization.yaml
nodes.summary: Kustomize overlay for the development environment that builds on `../../base` and applies two strategic-merge patches: the CORS-enabled Ambassador Mapping and the dev-encrypted database-connection SealedSecret.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the legacy `bases` and `patchesStrategicMerge` fields; newer Kustomize versions prefer `resources` and `patches`.

nodes.name: mapping.yaml
nodes.summary: Ambassador `getambassador.io/v2` Mapping patch for the `treetracker-tile-server` route in development that adds a permissive CORS policy: any origin, the GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/OPTIONS methods, and the Content-Type and Authorization headers.
nodes.languageNotes: As a strategic-merge patch, the file only adds `spec.cors`; the base Mapping keeps the `/tiles/` prefix, service target, rewrite, and timeout settings.

nodes.name: database-connection-sealed-secret.yaml
nodes.summary: Bitnami SealedSecret for production that stores the encrypted `db` key of the `database-connection` secret in the `tile-server` namespace. The in-cluster sealed-secrets controller decrypts it into the PostgreSQL connection string that the tile server container reads as DB_URL.
nodes.languageNotes: SealedSecrets are encrypted with the cluster controller's public key, so the ciphertext is safe to commit to git; only that cluster's controller can decrypt it.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Production strategic-merge patch for the treetracker-tile-server Deployment that runs 2 replicas with a 100m CPU and 768Mi memory request, a 1536Mi memory limit, and deliberately no CPU limit, based on measured pod usage. It also sets the container env vars PORT 3000, PG_POOL_SIZE 20, CACHE_SIZE 10000, CACHE_EXPIRE 60000, zoom thresholds 15 and 6, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED 0, and DB_URL from the database-connection secret.
nodes.languageNotes: The comment above the env list describes capping glibc malloc arenas, but the list sets no MALLOC_ARENA_MAX variable, so that comment has no matching setting. NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 turns off TLS certificate checks for Node.js outbound connections.

nodes.name: kustomization.yaml
nodes.summary: Kustomize overlay for the production environment that builds on ../../base and applies deployment.yaml, mapping.yaml, and database-connection-sealed-secret.yaml as strategic merge patches.
nodes.languageNotes: The `bases` and `patchesStrategicMerge` fields are deprecated in Kustomize v5, which uses `resources` and `patches` instead.

nodes.name: mapping.yaml
nodes.summary: Production patch for the Ambassador (getambassador.io/v2) Mapping named treetracker-tile-server that turns off the request timeout (timeout_ms 0). It also limits CORS to GET requests from https://prod-k8s.treetracker.org with the Content-Type and Authorization headers.

nodes.name: database-connection-sealed-secret.yaml
nodes.summary: Bitnami SealedSecret patch for the test cluster that replaces the base PLACEHOLDER with the encrypted `db` value of the `database-connection` secret in the `tile-server` namespace. The sealed-secrets controller decrypts it into the PostgreSQL connection string that the base Deployment injects into the container as DB_URL.
nodes.languageNotes: A SealedSecret is encrypted with the public key of one cluster's sealed-secrets controller and is bound to its name and namespace by default, so this ciphertext is safe to commit and decrypts only as tile-server/database-connection in the test cluster.

nodes.name: deployment.yaml
nodes.summary: Test-environment strategic-merge patch for the treetracker-tile-server Deployment that scales it to 6 replicas (the base uses 1). It raises MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_USING_GLOBAL_DATASET to 8 (the base uses 6), so config.js renders from the global dataset up to zoom 8, and keeps MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET at 6.
nodes.languageNotes: Strategic merge patches merge the containers list and the env list by their `name` keys, so this patch replaces only the two zoom variables and keeps the other base env vars (PORT, PG_POOL_SIZE, cache settings, DB_URL).

nodes.name: kustomization.yaml
nodes.summary: Kustomize overlay for the test environment that builds on ../../base and applies mapping.yaml, database-connection-sealed-secret.yaml, and deployment.yaml as strategic merge patches. The deploy-test.yml workflow runs `kustomize build deployment/overlays/test` and applies the result to the tile-server namespace.
nodes.languageNotes: The `bases` and `patchesStrategicMerge` fields are deprecated in current Kustomize releases, which use `resources` and `patches` for the same purpose.

nodes.name: mapping.yaml
nodes.summary: Test-environment patch for the Ambassador (getambassador.io/v2) Mapping named treetracker-tile-server that adds a CORS policy. It allows only GET requests from https://test-k8s.treetracker.org with the Content-Type and Authorization headers; the base Mapping still supplies the /tiles/ prefix route to the service.

nodes.name: stylesheet.xml
nodes.summary: Mapnik XML map definition in Web Mercator with a steelblue background: a white world_merc.shp shapefile base layer plus a WGS84 GeoJSON layer that reads ./trees.json and draws every tree point with ./images/pin_29px.png at 0.1 opacity. It also defines simplestyle-like polygon and line rules driven by feature attributes such as [fill] and [stroke].
nodes.languageNotes: Mapnik resolves the relative datasource and marker paths (world_merc.shp, ./trees.json, ./images/pin_29px.png) against the directory of the XML file, so the file only works from greenstand/. The layer srs string ends with a stray '<>' token, and two inline GeoJSON datasource alternatives are commented out.

nodes.name: stylesheet2.xml
nodes.summary: Variant of the Greenstand Mapnik stylesheet with the same Web Mercator map, world_merc.shp base layer, and pin_29px.png point style, but its GeoJSON layer embeds two inline CDATA points at [-10,10] and [-10,20] instead of reading trees.json. config.pg.test.js loads it to render a 512x512 PNG for tile z=2, x=1, y=1.

nodes.name: trees.json
nodes.summary: 53 MB GeoJSON FeatureCollection of 547,448 property-less Point features (one per line, [lon, lat] in WGS84) that snapshot real Treetracker tree locations, about 52% in East Africa around Tanzania and 23% in West Africa near Sierra Leone. stylesheet.xml renders it as a Mapnik GeoJSON layer, and the skipped seed test in db.test.js inserts up to about 10,000 of its points into the PostGIS trees3 table.
nodes.languageNotes: Points span longitude -162.6 to 174.2 and latitude -41.2 to 66.9 with only 268,086 distinct coordinates; one coordinate (37.510118, -2.967832) repeats 1,897 times, so many trees share identical GPS fixes.

nodes.name: trees_sample.json
nodes.summary: Three-feature GeoJSON FeatureCollection that copies the first three Point features of trees.json (Tanzania coordinates near 37.60E, 3.18S and 36.63E, 3.26S, with one duplicate point). db.test.js names it in a commented-out require as a small alternative seed input.

nodes.name: build_against_sdk.sh
nodes.summary: Builds node-mapnik from source against a prebuilt Mapnik SDK tarball (mapnik-<platform>-sdk-<mapnik_version>.tar.bz2) that it copies from a local mapnik-packaging output or downloads from mapnik.s3.amazonaws.com into sdk/. It then runs npm install --build-from-source with rpath and C++11 ABI flags, copies mapnik-index, shapeindex, libmapnik, input plugins and share data into the node-pre-gyp module path, and writes a mapnik_settings.js there.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a `: '...'` no-op heredoc as a block comment and parameter expansion defaults such as ${MAPNIK_GIT:-...} so callers can override the SDK version.

nodes.name: clang-format.sh
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the mason toolchain through setup.sh, installs clang-format at MASON_LLVM_RELEASE, and reformats every .cpp and .hpp file under src/ in place with the repo style file. It exits 1 and prints a git diff when any file under src/ changed, so CI can flag unformatted C++ code.

nodes.name: clang-tidy.sh
nodes.summary: Installs clang-tidy through mason, generates build/compile_commands.json by piping a clean make run into generate_compile_commands.py when the file is missing, and runs run-clang-tidy.py -fix from the build directory. It exits 1 with a git diff when clang-tidy auto-fixed any file under src/.

nodes.name: coverage.sh
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the native module in debug mode with clang -fprofile-instr-generate and -fcoverage-mapping, runs npm test with LLVM_PROFILE_FILE set, and merges the code-*.profraw files into code.profdata. It then prints an llvm-cov report and source listing for src/*.cpp and writes an HTML report to /tmp/coverage.html.

nodes.name: create_scheme.sh
nodes.summary: Generates an Xcode .xcscheme file inside build/binding.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes by filling the {{BLUEPRINT_ID}}, {{BUILDABLE_NAME}}, {{NODE_PATH}}, {{NODE_ARGUMENT}} and other placeholders of the scripts/<SCHEME_TYPE>.xcscheme template from environment variables. It reuses an existing 24-character BlueprintIdentifier when the scheme already exists, or generates a random one from /dev/urandom.

nodes.name: install_deps.sh
nodes.summary: Installs and links the pinned mason packages that Mapnik needs (jpeg_turbo, libpng, libtiff, icu 57.1, proj, pixman, cairo, webp, libgdal, boost 1.74.0 libraries, freetype, harfbuzz) and then Mapnik itself at commit c6fc956a7. It skips all installs when mason_packages/.link/bin/mapnik-config already exists.

nodes.name: install_node.sh
nodes.summary: Installs the Node.js version given as the first argument by cloning nvm into ./__nvm, sourcing it, and running nvm install and nvm use, after it unloads any nvm that is already active. It prints the node and npm versions so CI logs show which runtime the build uses.

nodes.name: is_pr_merge.sh
nodes.summary: Detects a Travis CI pull-request merge commit by comparing the latest non-merge commit message from git log with the HEAD message from git show. It prints true when the two messages differ, which means HEAD is a synthetic merge commit such as 'Merge e3b1981 into 615d2a3'.

nodes.name: package_osx.sh
nodes.summary: Legacy macOS release script that installs node-pre-gyp and aws-sdk under Node 0.10 and then builds, tests, packages and publishes node-mapnik binaries for Node 0.10.33 and 0.11.14. It switches back to Node 0.10 at the end to avoid an npm publish problem with Node 0.11.

nodes.name: doit
nodes.summary: Builds node-mapnik for one Node version: it switches nvm to that version, sources build_against_sdk.sh with --target, runs npm test, and runs node-pre-gyp package, testpackage and publish to upload the binary. It then deletes build/ and lib/binding and reinstalls with --fallback-to-build=false to verify that the published binary installs and passes tests.

nodes.name: postinstall.sh
nodes.summary: Post-build action (run from binding.gyp) that writes lib/binding/mapnik_settings.js with the font, input plugin, mapnik-index, shapeindex, ICU, GDAL and PROJ paths that lib/mapnik.js loads at runtime. With a source-installed Mapnik it takes the paths from mapnik-config; with the mason package it copies the binaries, libmapnik, plugins and gdal/proj/icu data into lib/binding to make a portable package and uses __dirname-relative paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the bash `-ef` test to check that `which mapnik-config` resolves to the same file as the mason copy, and switches between `cp -r` (macOS) and `cp -rL` (Linux) to dereference symlinks.

nodes.name: publish.sh
nodes.summary: CI publish step that prints node-pre-gyp binary metadata and uploads the compiled binary to S3 only when the last commit message contains [publish binary] (package publish) or [republish binary] (package unpublish publish). It skips publishing for Travis PR merge commits and forwards all arguments, such as --debug and --toolset, to node-pre-gyp.

nodes.name: is_pr_merge
nodes.summary: Compares COMMIT_MESSAGE (the last non-merge git log message) with the HEAD message from git show and echoes true when they differ. publish uses this result to recognize a Travis CI PR merge commit.

nodes.name: publish
nodes.summary: Runs node-pre-gyp reveal, then chooses the publish action from the commit message: node-pre-gyp package publish for [publish binary], package unpublish publish for [republish binary], or a skip message otherwise. It also skips when is_pr_merge reports a PR merge commit.

nodes.name: sanitize.sh
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the native module in debug mode with the MASON_SANITIZE_CXXFLAGS and MASON_SANITIZE_LDFLAGS (AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer) from local.env and runs the tape tests with the clang ASan runtime preloaded. On macOS it calls node and tape directly with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES; on Linux it runs npm test with LD_PRELOAD.

nodes.name: setup.sh
nodes.summary: Toolchain bootstrap script that, when called as setup.sh --config <file>, prepares clang++ (MASON_LLVM_RELEASE 10.0.0) and the mason package manager (MASON_RELEASE 03a3ea40) and writes a sourceable env file such as local.env. The other developer scripts (clang-format, clang-tidy, coverage, sanitize, install_deps) source that file to get PATH, CXX, mason versions and sanitizer settings.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Selects a global mason clang++ or llvm install under ~/.mason when one exists, or else downloads the clang++ tarball from the mason-binaries S3 bucket into .toolchain, and downloads mason into .mason. It then writes export lines for PATH, CXX, MASON_LLVM_RT_PRELOAD, ASAN/UBSAN/LSAN options and MASON_SANITIZE flags into the config file, and writes leak suppressions to /tmp/leak_suppressions.txt.

nodes.name: setup_cpp11_toolchain.sh
nodes.summary: Legacy script, meant to be sourced, that bootstraps a C++11 toolchain on Ubuntu precise or trusty. It downloads clang 3.5 and libstdc++ 4.8 .deb packages, extracts them into ./toolchain, and exports CXX, CC, PATH, CPLUS_INCLUDE_PATH and library paths. On non-Linux systems it does nothing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Checks that the host is Ubuntu, reads the release codename with lsb_release, and uses the nested dpack helper to wget and dpkg -x the matching clang-3.5, libllvm3.5 and libstdc++-4.8 packages from llvm.org and the ubuntu-toolchain-r PPA. It then exports the include, library, PATH, CXX and CC variables, and exits 1 for unsupported distros.

nodes.name: show_module_runtime.ps1
nodes.summary: Windows PowerShell check that recursively finds every .node binary under the directory given as the first argument and runs dumpbin /DEPENDENTS on each one. It reports whether each module links VCRUNTIME140.dll and prints the full dependency list in red for modules that do not.

nodes.name: ubuntu_ppa_tests.sh
nodes.summary: Legacy Ubuntu test script that adds the mapnik v2.2.0, nightly-2.3 and nightly-trunk PPAs and, in turn, installs libmapnik 2.2.0, 2.3.0 and 3.0.0 packages. For each version it rebuilds node-mapnik with npm install --build-from-source and runs npm test, and it purges the old packages before it installs the next version.

nodes.name: validate_tag.sh
nodes.summary: Travis CI guard that, when HEAD is on a git tag equal to TRAVIS_BRANCH, reads the version field from package.json and exits 1 when neither <version> nor v<version> matches the tag. It catches releases that were tagged without a version bump in package.json.

nodes.name: initialize.sh
nodes.summary: One-time bootstrap of a local PostGIS cluster from mason binaries: it sources mason-postgis-config.env, creates the PGHOST socket and PGTEMP_DIR directories, runs initdb, and starts postgres in the background. It then adds a temp_disk tablespace and plpythonu, creates the template_postgis database with the postgis, hstore, fuzzystrmatch, and unaccent extensions, and stops the server with pg_ctl.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses set -eu with pipefail so any failed psql or initdb step aborts the bootstrap, and sleep 2 pauses to let the backgrounded postgres process accept connections.

nodes.name: run.sh
nodes.summary: Starts the already-initialized local mason PostGIS server in the background on the PGHOST Unix socket, with output to postgres.log. It exits with an error if mason-postgis-config.env is missing and prints the pg_ctl command that stops the server.

nodes.name: setup.sh
nodes.summary: Installs libgdal 2.1.3 and postgis 2.3.2-1 with the mason package manager, links postgis into mason_packages/.link, and checks that the GDAL share/gdal data directory exists. It then writes mason-postgis-config.env, which exports PGDATA, PGHOST, PGTEMP_DIR, PGPORT=1111, PATH, and GDAL_DATA for the other PostGIS scripts.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-quoted echo lines write literal ${CURRENT_DIR} references into the env file so they expand when the file is sourced, while the double-quoted GDAL_DATA line expands at generation time.

nodes.name: setup_and_run.sh
nodes.summary: Four-line wrapper that the legacy Travis CI jobs source to get a running local PostGIS: it calls setup.sh, initialize.sh, and run.sh in order, then sources mason-postgis-config.env into the calling shell.
nodes.languageNotes: Has no shebang because it is meant to be sourced, so the final source of the env file leaves PGHOST, PGPORT, and PATH set in the caller's shell.

nodes.name: stop.sh
nodes.summary: Shuts down the local mason PostGIS server: it sources mason-postgis-config.env to locate PGDATA and runs mason_packages/.link/bin/pg_ctl -w stop, which waits until the server exits.

nodes.name: .clang-format
nodes.summary: clang-format style file (the Mapbox.Variant C++ style) for the upstream node-mapnik C++ sources: 4-space indent, no tabs, no column limit, braces on new lines after classes and functions, left pointer alignment, C++11, and include sorting off. scripts/clang-format.sh applies it with -style=file to every .cpp and .hpp file under src/.

nodes.name: .clang-tidy
nodes.summary: clang-tidy configuration that enables only the clang-analyzer-* checks (minus the macOS and optin UninitializedObject checks), treats every warning as an error, and limits header diagnostics to paths that match /src/. scripts/clang-tidy.sh runs these checks over the upstream C++ binding code.

nodes.name: .gitattributes
nodes.summary: Git attributes file that marks the world_merc.json and world_merc.converted.geojson fixtures as text with LF line endings, so that these GeoJSON fixtures keep the same bytes on every platform.

nodes.name: .gitmodules
nodes.summary: Git submodule map that pins three Mapbox header-only C++ libraries into deps/: wagyu (polygon clipping), geometry.hpp, and protozero (protobuf decoding). binding.gyp adds their include/ folders, and the Makefile fetches them with git submodule update --init.

nodes.name: .huskyrc
nodes.summary: Husky v4 hook configuration that runs commitlint -E HUSKY_GIT_PARAMS on every commit-msg event, so that each commit message is checked against the Conventional Commits rules from commitlint.config.js.

nodes.name: .npmignore
nodes.summary: npm packaging exclude list that keeps build output (lib/binding, build), tests, benchmarks, docs, CI files (.travis.yml, appveyor.yml), mason toolchain folders, vcbuild.bat, local PostGIS artifacts (local-postgres, postgres.log, local.env), and the deps/ submodule tests and docs out of the published npm tarball.

nodes.name: .releaserc
nodes.summary: semantic-release configuration that releases from master and publishes prereleases from next with the commit-analyzer, release-notes-generator, changelog, npm, git, and github plugins; the git plugin commits docs, package.json, and CHANGELOG.md as 'chore(release): <version> [skip ci]'. The build-deploy GitHub Actions workflow runs semantic-release with this file.

nodes.name: mapnik-index.js
nodes.summary: CLI shim (the mapnik-index.js bin entry in package.json) that finds the native binding folder through @mapbox/node-pre-gyp, spawns the bundled mapnik-index executable from its bin/ folder (or mapnik-index on PATH), forwards the arguments and stdio, and exits with the child's exit code.

nodes.name: mapnik-inspect.js
nodes.summary: Upstream node-mapnik inspection CLI that picks a handler from the input file extension: it opens shapefile, CSV/TSV, OSM, SQLite, GeoJSON, OGR (KML/GML/DBF), and GDAL raster files as mapnik.Datasource objects and prints their description, extent, and feature count. It also prints VectorTile.info for .mvt/.vector.pbf, renders .svg to /tmp/mapnik-inspect.png, dumps place_label attributes from .xml stylesheets, parses .prj files with srs, and prints .zip contents.

nodes.name: mapnik-render.js
nodes.summary: Upstream node-mapnik render CLI (render.js <stylesheet> <image>) that loads a Mapnik XML stylesheet in strict mode into a 600x400 map, zooms to all layers, writes the image file, and tries to open it. For a .mml CartoCSS project it first compiles the project to XML with the optional carto package.

nodes.name: mapnik-shapeindex.js
nodes.summary: CLI shim (the mapnik-shapeindex.js bin entry) that resolves the node-pre-gyp binding path and runs the bundled shapeindex executable (or shapeindex on PATH) to build spatial indexes for shapefiles; it pipes stdout and stderr, propagates the exit code, and throws 'shapeindex not found' when the binary is missing.

nodes.name: binding.gyp
nodes.summary: node-gyp build definition for the native mapnik addon: it compiles the src/*.cpp N-API wrappers plus the mapnik-vector-tile sources into <(module_path), and takes include paths, defines, and libraries from mapnik-config and the deps/ submodules, with per-OS settings for MSVC, Linux rpath, and Xcode C++14. It also adds glibc_workaround.cpp and SSE_MATH through variables, and its action_after_build target runs scripts/postinstall.sh on non-Windows hosts.
nodes.languageNotes: GYP files are Python-literal dictionaries: '<!@(cmd)' expands a shell command into a list at configure time, a trailing '%' on a variable makes it a default that the command line can override, and keys that end in '!' remove items from an inherited list.
