nodes.name: commitlint.config.js
nodes.summary: One-line commitlint configuration that extends @commitlint/config-conventional, so that the husky commit-msg hook rejects commit messages that do not follow the Conventional Commits format.

nodes.name: common.gypi
nodes.summary: Shared gyp target_defaults that binding.gyp includes: it makes Release the default configuration, compiles with -std=c++14 with RTTI and exceptions on, and defines Debug (no NDEBUG, -O0, debug symbols) and Release (NDEBUG, -O3, dead-code stripping) settings for Xcode and for MSVC (v140 toolset, /MP, /bigobj, /MD).

nodes.name: XMLConfig.js
nodes.summary: Holds a hard-coded Mapnik XML map template for clustered tree markers (cluster_46px.png icon with a [count] text label in DejaVu Serif Condensed Bold Italic) over a PostGIS layer on the trees table of treetracker_dev, and exports the XMLConfig class that swaps the layer SQL. No server module requires it; only XMLConfig.test.js uses it.

nodes.name: XMLConfig.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest test that creates an XMLConfig, calls select with 'select * from tree2', and checks that the toString() output now contains that SQL.

nodes.name: app.test.js
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder test file (0 bytes) next to the Express tile app; it has no test cases, so Jest (npm run jest) reports it as a failed suite that must contain at least one test.

nodes.name: db.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest 'seed' suite that writes points into a local PostGIS database (postgres@172.17.0.4, database treetracker) through knex: the active case clears trees4 and inserts a 7-degree lon/lat grid, and the skipped case loads up to 10,000 points from trees.json into trees3. Both cases then set estimated_geometric_location with ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(lon, lat), 4326).

nodes.name: postgis.xml
nodes.summary: Mapnik XML stylesheet template for the tile server: a Web Mercator map with a pin_29px.png point style (layer0, interactive on id) over layer l1, a PostGIS datasource that selects active trees ordered by id DESC from treetracker_dev with geometry column estimated_geometric_location. config.js reads it, substitutes host, port, user, password, and database from DB_URL, and writes layers/postgis.prod.xml.
nodes.languageNotes: The literal connection values (172.17.0.2, 5432, postgres, greenstand, treetracker_dev) are placeholders that config.js replaces with regexes. configFreetown in config.js searches for '(SELECT * FROM trees) as cdbq', but this file uses a different table subquery, so that replacement does not match.

nodes.name: SQLTree.js
nodes.summary: Builds parameterized PostgreSQL queries for one tree's detail record: the SQLTree class joins trees with planter, tree_species, wallet.token, and wallet.wallet to add the species name, planter name and image, token UUID, and wallet name. No server module requires it; only SQLTree.test.js uses it.

nodes.name: SQLTree.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest test (with an empty test name) that sets tree ID 1 and matches getQuery() output against a regex that expects 'left join token' and 'left join entity' clauses. The current query joins wallet.token and has no entity join, so this assertion fails.

nodes.name: trees_sample.geojson
nodes.summary: Three-point GeoJSON FeatureCollection near 37.6E, 3.2S in northern Tanzania (the first and third points are duplicates, and no feature has properties); experimental.test.js uses it as a file-based geojson datasource in its rendering experiment.

nodes.name: trees_text.geojson
nodes.summary: Single-feature GeoJSON fixture with one point at [0,0] and the property sss = '2k'; font.test.js loads it as a geojson datasource to test text label rendering with registered fonts.

nodes.name: utils.js
nodes.summary: Exports setSql, a string helper that rewrites the table subquery in a Mapnik PostGIS table Parameter (the CDATA[(...) as cdbq] block) to a new SQL statement. Only utils.test.js uses it; the server does not require it.

nodes.name: utils.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest test that runs setSql on a multi-line PostGIS table Parameter and checks that the result contains the new 'select * from ddd' SQL.

nodes.name: meta
nodes.summary: Prints a datasource's describe() output and extent, then walks its featureset with next() to count and print the number of features; mapnik-inspect.js calls it for every datasource-backed file type.

nodes.name: XMLConfig
nodes.summary: Wraps the cluster map template string: the constructor copies the template, select(sentence) replaces the literal '(SELECT * FROM trees) as cdbq' table subquery with the given SQL, and toString() returns the resulting XML.

nodes.name: SQLTree
nodes.summary: Stateful query builder with setTreeId/getQuery for lookup by numeric trees.id and setTreeUUID/getQueryUUID for lookup by trees.uuid; each getter throws when its key is unset and returns a { text, values } object for the pg driver.

nodes.name: getQuery
nodes.summary: Returns the { text, values: [treeId] } query that selects an active tree by trees.id with the joined species name, planter first/last name and image_url, token id as token_uuid, and wallet name; it throws 'treeId required' when no ID is set and logs the query.

nodes.name: getQueryUUID
nodes.summary: Variant of the tree detail query that filters on trees.uuid = $1 with the UUID from setTreeUUID; it throws 'treeUUID required' when that UUID is missing and logs the { text, values } object before it returns it.

nodes.name: setSql
nodes.summary: Replaces the multi-line 'CDATA[(...) as cdbq]' table subquery in the given XML string with 'CDATA[(<sql>) as cdbq]' through a dotAll regex and returns the new string.

nodes.name: generate_compile_commands.py
nodes.summary: Reads verbose `make` output from stdin, keeps the compiler lines that contain NODE_GYP_MODULE_NAME, and prints a clang JSON compilation database (directory, command, file) for the node-gyp `build/` directory to stdout.
nodes.languageNotes: The regex `^(.*) (.+cpp)\n` assumes that each compile line ends with the .cpp source path. A line that has the token but does not match makes `match.group(2)` raise AttributeError.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Iterates over the stdin lines, builds one {directory, command, file} record per node-gyp compile line with the source path normalized against `<cwd>/build`, and dumps the list as indented JSON.

nodes.name: library.xcscheme
nodes.summary: Xcode scheme template (format version 1.3) for the node-mapnik library target, with {{BLUEPRINT_ID}}, {{BUILDABLE_NAME}}, {{BLUEPRINT_NAME}} and {{CONTAINER}} placeholders; it uses Debug for test, launch and analyze, and Release for profile and archive.

nodes.name: node.xcscheme
nodes.summary: Xcode scheme template that launches {{NODE_PATH}}/node with {{NODE_ARGUMENT}} in {{WORKING_DIRECTORY}} and prepends {{NODE_PATH}} to PATH, so a developer can debug the native addon under LLDB while a Node.js script runs it.

nodes.name: glibc_workaround.cpp
nodes.summary: Linux-only shim, compiled when MAPNIK_ENABLE_GLIBC_WORKAROUND is defined, that supplies its own std::__throw_out_of_range_fmt so the addon can be built with libstdc++ 4.9 without a runtime dependency on the GLIBCXX_3.4.20 symbol version.
nodes.languageNotes: A definition inside namespace std is normally undefined behavior. Here it is a deliberate link-time override: the local definition satisfies the references that the libstdc++ 4.9 headers emit.

nodes.name: __throw_out_of_range_fmt
nodes.summary: Replacement for the libstdc++ formatted out_of_range thrower: it ignores the printf-style arguments and calls std::__throw_out_of_range with the raw format string; it is declared __noreturn__.

nodes.name: mapnik_grid.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the N-API `mapnik.Grid` class (only when GRID_RENDERER is defined): it builds a mapnik::grid hit buffer from width, height and an optional `key` (default `__id__`), and offers field registration, clear, sub-views, and sync or async encoding into UTFGrid JSON with `grid`, `keys` and `data` members.
nodes.languageNotes: Each async method pairs a JS-facing wrapper with a Napi::AsyncWorker subclass. Execute() runs on the libuv thread pool and does not touch JS values; GetResult() builds the JS callback arguments back on the main thread.

nodes.name: AsyncGridClear
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that clears the shared mapnik::grid off the main thread and then passes the callback a new JS Grid object that wraps the same grid_ptr.

nodes.name: AsyncGridClear::GetResult
nodes.summary: Wraps the cleared grid_ptr in a Napi::External and calls Grid::constructor.New to return (null, Grid) to the JS callback; without a grid it falls back to the AsyncWorker default result.

nodes.name: AsyncGridEncode
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that holds the grid_ptr, the resolution and the feature flag, runs grid2utf on a worker thread, and stores the encoded UTF lines and key order for the callback.

nodes.name: AsyncGridEncode::Execute
nodes.summary: Calls node_mapnik::grid2utf<mapnik::grid> on the worker thread to fill lines_ and key_order_ at the requested resolution, and turns any std::exception into a callback error with SetError.

nodes.name: AsyncGridEncode::GetResult
nodes.summary: On the main thread, converts key_order_ into a JS array, optionally fills feature attributes with write_features<mapnik::grid>, and returns (null, {grid, keys, data}) to the Grid.encode callback.

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.summary: Registers the `Grid` JS class with DefineClass (key accessor; encode/encodeSync, clear/clearSync, painted, fields, addField, view, width, height; static base_mask), keeps a persistent constructor reference, and sets `exports.Grid`.

nodes.name: Grid
nodes.summary: JS constructor for Grid: it adopts an existing grid_ptr when it gets one Napi::External; otherwise it validates numeric width and height plus an optional options object with a string `key`, and allocates a new mapnik::grid. Bad arguments throw TypeError or Error.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Clears the grid synchronously through clearSync when it gets no arguments; otherwise it requires a trailing callback function and queues an AsyncGridClear worker.

nodes.name: key
nodes.summary: Getter and setter pair behind the `grid.key` JS property: the getter returns the join key string of the grid, and the setter calls set_key after a check that the new value is a string.

nodes.name: addField
nodes.summary: Adds one attribute name to the output field set of the grid through mapnik::grid::add_field; it throws TypeError unless it gets exactly one string argument.

nodes.name: fields
nodes.summary: Copies the std::set of field names that are registered on the mapnik::grid into a new JS array and returns it through an EscapableHandleScope.

nodes.name: view
nodes.summary: Creates a GridView over the x, y, width, height window of this grid: it passes an External grid_ptr and the four numbers to GridView::constructor.New. Its argument check joins the IsNumber tests with &&, so it rejects only calls where all four arguments are non-numeric.

nodes.name: encodeSync
nodes.summary: Synchronously encodes the full grid to UTFGrid JSON: it validates the options `resolution` (non-zero integer, default 4) and `features` (boolean, default true although the doc comment says false), runs grid2utf and write_features, and returns {grid, keys, data}.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Async counterpart of Grid.encodeSync: it applies the same `resolution` and `features` option checks, requires a trailing callback function, and queues an AsyncGridEncode worker.

nodes.name: mapnik_grid_view.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the N-API `mapnik.GridView` class (only when GRID_RENDERER is defined), a rectangular window over a parent mapnik::grid that JS code can get only from Grid.view(); it offers width, height, fields, getPixel, sync and async isSolid, and sync and async UTFGrid encoding.
nodes.languageNotes: The option parsing for `resolution` and `features` is copied verbatim into encodeSync and encode here and again in mapnik_grid.cpp, so a fix to the option validation must be applied in four places.

nodes.name: AsyncIsSolid
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that scans every row of a grid_view on a worker thread to decide whether all pixels share the feature id of the first pixel, and returns (null, solid) plus that pixel value when the view is solid.

nodes.name: AsyncIsSolid::Execute
nodes.summary: Compares each grid_view value with the value at (0,0) and stops at the first difference; a view with zero width or height becomes a 'grid_view does not have valid dimensions' error, while isSolidSync returns true for that case.

nodes.name: AsyncGridViewEncode
nodes.summary: Napi::AsyncWorker that encodes a grid_view (not the whole parent grid) to UTF lines with grid2utf<mapnik::grid_view>, and keeps the key order and the feature flag for the callback result.

nodes.name: AsyncGridViewEncode::Execute
nodes.summary: Runs node_mapnik::grid2utf<mapnik::grid_view> on the thread pool for the window of the view at resolution_, and reports any std::exception to the callback through SetError.

nodes.name: AsyncGridViewEncode::GetResult
nodes.summary: Builds the GridView encode result on the main thread: a JS keys array from key_order_, optional feature data from write_features<mapnik::grid_view>, and the grid line strings, returned as (null, {grid, keys, data}).

nodes.name: Initialize
nodes.summary: Registers the `GridView` JS class with eight instance methods (encodeSync, encode, fields, width, height, isSolid, isSolidSync, getPixel), stores the persistent constructor that Grid.view uses, and sets `exports.GridView`.

nodes.name: GridView
nodes.summary: Accepts only an External grid_ptr plus four numbers (x, y, w, h), keeps the parent grid_ptr alive in grid_, and wraps grid_->get_view(x, y, w, h) in a shared mapnik::grid_view; any other call throws 'Cannot create this object from Javascript'.

nodes.name: fields
nodes.summary: Returns the field names of the underlying grid_view as a JS array, which it fills from the std::set that get_fields() gives.

nodes.name: isSolid
nodes.summary: Delegates to isSolidSync when it gets no arguments; otherwise it checks that the last argument is a callback function and queues an AsyncIsSolid worker over grid_view_.

nodes.name: isSolidSync
nodes.summary: Synchronously reports whether every value in the grid view equals the top-left value, and returns true for an empty view.

nodes.name: getPixel
nodes.summary: Returns the grid_view value (the feature id) at integer coordinates x, y, returns undefined for out-of-bounds coordinates, and throws TypeError when x or y is missing or is not a number.

nodes.name: encodeSync
nodes.summary: Synchronously encodes only the view window into UTFGrid JSON with the same `resolution` (default 4, non-zero) and `features` (default true) options as Grid.encodeSync, and returns {grid, keys, data}; a std::exception becomes a JS Error.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Callback form of GridView.encodeSync: it validates the same options, requires the last argument to be a function, and queues an AsyncGridViewEncode worker for the view.

nodes.name: mapnik_grid_view.hpp
nodes.summary: Header (GRID_RENDERER builds only) that declares the GridView N-API wrapper and the grid_view_ptr alias for std::shared_ptr<mapnik::grid_view>; it includes mapnik_grid.hpp and makes Grid a friend so that Grid.view can construct views.

nodes.name: GridView
nodes.summary: Napi::ObjectWrap<GridView> declaration with a static Initialize, a CallbackInfo constructor, the encode, encodeSync, fields, width, height, isSolid, isSolidSync and getPixel methods, an impl() accessor, and private grid_view_ and parent grid_ shared pointers.

nodes.name: cpp.el
nodes.summary: Emacs Lisp helper that defines the `fixup` command, which tools/fix_cpp_style.sh runs in batch mode to reformat C++ sources with BSD style and 4-space indentation.

nodes.name: fixup
nodes.summary: Sets c-set-style "bsd", zero indentation inside namespaces, template-argument continuation lineup and c-basic-offset 4, then reindents the whole buffer, converts tabs to spaces, deletes trailing whitespace and saves the file.

nodes.name: fix_cpp_style.sh
nodes.summary: Shell loop that finds every file under ./src/ and runs `emacs -batch <file> -l $(pwd)/tools/cpp.el -f fixup` on it, so it must run from the repository root; it has no shebang and does not quote $file, so paths with spaces break it.

layers.name: Tile Server API
layers.description: server.js loads .env and starts the Express app in app.js, which renders 256x256 PNG tiles and UTF grid JSON tiles at /:z/:x/:y and /new/:z/:x/:y and answers every other path with a version banner.

layers.name: Tile Style Service
layers.description: config.js turns each tile request into a Mapnik XML style by filling the xml.js and xml2.js icon templates with tree GeoJSON or PostGIS SQL, with sphericalmercator.js for the tile bounding box and layers/postgis.xml as the DB_URL credential template.

layers.name: Tree Query And Cache
layers.description: Map.js picks one of the greenstand/sqls query builders by map mode and zoom (region clusters, tree points, on-the-fly or precomputed clusters, zoom targets, and timeline, wallet, and organization variants), and PGPool.js runs these PostGIS queries with an LRU cache that also merges identical concurrent queries.

layers.name: Tile Server Tests And Fixtures
layers.description: Jest suites for the greenstand/ modules (several are stale or need a live PostGIS) together with the sample tree GeoJSON files, including the 547,448-point trees.json, and the sample Mapnik stylesheets that these tests and experiments load.

layers.name: Mapnik JS Loader And CLIs
layers.description: lib/mapnik.js is the package main that loads the compiled node-mapnik addon through node-pre-gyp and adds the font and plugin helpers that the tile server imports, lib/index.js re-exports it, and the bin/ CLIs wrap mapnik-index, shapeindex, datasource inspection, and stylesheet rendering.

layers.name: Native Mapnik Binding
layers.description: Upstream node-mapnik C++ N-API wrappers in src/ that node_mapnik.cpp registers to expose Mapnik Map rendering, Image and blend operations, UTF Grid, VectorTile, Datasource, Feature, Geometry, and Projection classes to JavaScript.

layers.name: Native Build And Dev Tooling
layers.description: The upstream Makefile, binding.gyp, and common.gypi compile the addon against a mason Mapnik SDK, and scripts/ and tools/ hold the upstream helpers for dependency install, clang-format and clang-tidy, coverage, sanitizers, Xcode schemes, binary publishing, and a local PostGIS for tests.

layers.name: Container And Kubernetes Deployment
layers.description: The Dockerfile builds the tile server image on the greenstand/tile-server-base image, and deployment/ holds the kustomize base (Deployment, Service, Ambassador Mapping, and the SealedSecret that supplies DB_URL) with beta, development, production, and test overlays.

layers.name: Release And Deploy Pipelines
layers.description: GitHub Actions workflows run semantic-release from .releaserc, push the image to DockerHub, and apply the kustomize overlays to the DigitalOcean clusters, and the legacy upstream .travis.yml keeps the old native build matrix.

layers.name: Project Config And Docs
layers.description: The package.json manifest (start script, dependencies, and node-pre-gyp binary block), the .env runtime settings, the Prettier, commitlint, and husky settings, and the README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE, and index.html pages, most of which come from upstream node-mapnik.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README is titled treetracker-tile-server (previously node-mapnik-1), but most of its text is still upstream node-mapnik documentation: examples that render a Mapnik stylesheet to a PNG, convert a JPEG to PNG, and build the native addon with make release or make release_base. It does not describe the Greenstand tile server, so read package.json next to see the two halves of this fork. The manifest sets main to ./lib/mapnik.js (the Mapnik bindings), its start script runs greenstand/server.js (the Express tile server), and its install step fetches or builds the native binding through node-pre-gyp.

tour.title: Server Entry Point
tour.description: greenstand/server.js is the process that the start script from Step 1 launches. It loads .env through dotenv, sets the log level to info, asserts that MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_USING_GLOBAL_DATASET and MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET are defined, and then starts the Express app from app.js on PORT. The local .env supplies these values: PORT=23300, a 10000-entry query cache, a PG_POOL_SIZE of 60, and 6 for both zoom thresholds. Step 6 shows how the zoom-target threshold changes the cluster query.
tour.languageLesson: dotenv copies the KEY=value lines of a .env file into process.env when the process starts. By default it does not overwrite a variable that is already set, so values from the runtime environment (for example, container env vars) take precedence over the file. All process.env values are strings.

tour.title: Express Tile Routes
tour.description: app.js builds the Express application: it creates a pg Pool from DB_URL and PG_POOL_SIZE, builds a Config object, and registers the Mapnik fonts and input plugins. Its tile routes render a 256x256 tile through buildMapInstance and return either a PNG image or a UTF grid JSON with the id, latlon, count, and type fields (plus zoom_to at zoom 9 and below); a render error returns HTTP 500 with a JSON message. The /new routes add newIcons: true, which Config.getXMLString ignores, and a catch-all route answers every other path with a version banner from package.json.
tour.languageLesson: Express route patterns such as /:z/:x/:y.png capture URL segments into req.params, so one handler serves every tile coordinate. Express tries handlers in registration order, so a catch-all route such as ALL * must come after the specific routes to act as a fallback.

tour.title: Per-Tile Style Builder
tour.description: The Config object from Step 3 turns each tile request into a Mapnik XML style. It gets the SQL from Map.js; for zoom 1 to 15 it fetches the rows through PGPool and inlines them as GeoJSON, and for deeper zooms it injects the SQL and the DB_URL credentials into a PostGIS template. sphericalmercator.js supplies the tile geometry: it converts tiles to Web Mercator envelopes and gives a pixel-buffered lon/lat bounding box for the tile SQL queries. layers/postgis.xml is the PostGIS stylesheet template whose host, port, user, password, and database config.js replaces with the DB_URL values.
tour.languageLesson: Web Mercator is the projection of most web map tiles. At zoom z the world is a grid of 2^z by 2^z tiles of 256 pixels, and the projection stops at about +/-85.0511 degrees latitude, which is why sphericalmercator.js clips its lon/lat boxes there.

tour.title: Map Modes and Base Queries
tour.description: Map.js is the query planner behind config.js: it picks a SQL builder from greenstand/sqls by map mode (single tree, user, wallet, organization map_name, timeline, or default) and by zoom level, then runs the query on a pg pool. Four base builders cover the zoom range: SQLCase1 counts trees per region from active_tree_region, SQLCase3 clusters active trees on the fly with PostGIS ST_ClusterWithin, SQLCase4 reads precomputed clusters from the clusters table (Map.js uses it for default maps at zoom 12 to 15), and SQLCase2 returns individual tree points at high zoom. Most builders also accept optional filters such as planter, wallet, organization map_name, and bounding box.
tour.languageLesson: ST_ClusterWithin(geom, distance) is a PostGIS aggregate that groups geometries that lie within a given distance of each other. When the distance depends on the zoom level, as in SQLCase3, clusters keep a similar size on screen at every zoom.

tour.title: Specialized Query Variants
tour.description: Specialized map modes extend the base builders from Step 5 instead of copying them. SQLCase1WithZoomTarget, the most referenced builder, adds a zoom_to centroid to each region cluster at zoom levels up to MAXIMUM_ZOOM_LEVEL_HANDLING_ZOOM_TARGET (the threshold that server.js checks in Step 2), and SQLZoomTargetCase1 finds that centroid as the most populated subregion two zoom levels deeper. The Timeline variants keep only trees whose time_created falls in a 'YYYY-MM-DD_YYYY-MM-DD' range, and SQLCase2Wallet keeps only trees whose tokens belong to the named wallet. The UTF grid route from Step 3 lists zoom_to among its fields at zoom 9 and below.
tour.languageLesson: These builders use ES class inheritance: a subclass extends a base builder and overrides only the query parts that it changes, and it can throw for filters that it does not support (SQLCase2Wallet throws 'dedicated'). Some builders return a pg {text, values} object instead of a plain string, which keeps user input in separate $1, $2 parameters rather than in the SQL text.

tour.title: Cached Query Pool
tour.description: PGPool wraps a pg Pool and puts an LRU cache in front of it, by default with 10000 entries and a 4-minute expiry. When several tile requests send the same SQL at the same time, PGPool merges them into one database query, and it caches each post-processed result. config.js from Step 4 uses it to cache the GeoJSON-filled Mapnik XML for each tile query, so a cache hit returns the finished XML for that query.
tour.languageLesson: A common way to merge identical concurrent requests is to cache the pending Promise for a key, not only the final value, so every caller that arrives before the query finishes awaits the same Promise. An LRU (least recently used) cache with a size limit and a maximum age bounds both memory use and data staleness.

tour.title: Mapnik XML Templates
tour.description: config.js builds its style by filling these template strings with tree GeoJSON or PostGIS SQL. xml.js holds the original orange-icon templates: PostGIS layers for clusters (cluster_46px and cluster_63px shields) and for single trees (pin_29px.png), plus xmlJson and xmlJsonForTree, which use an inline GeoJSON datasource with a json_data placeholder. xml2.js holds the green 'ptk' icon variants with Lato Regular labels and tree icons, and it derives xmlJson3 and xmlTree3 from them by regex replace.
tour.languageLesson: A Mapnik XML map pairs Style elements with Layer elements. A Style holds Rules with symbolizers such as PointSymbolizer (an icon) or ShieldSymbolizer (an icon with a text label). A Layer names its styles and holds a Datasource that tells Mapnik where the features come from, for example type postgis with an SQL subquery or type geojson with inline data.

tour.title: Mapnik JavaScript Loader
tour.description: The tile server imports Mapnik through lib/mapnik.js, the package main from Step 1, and app.js uses its font and plugin helpers. The loader finds the compiled native binding with @mapbox/node-pre-gyp, applies environment variables from mapnik_settings.js, registers MAPNIK_FONT_PATH fonts, and adds version information plus the typeName, toWKB, and toWKT prototype helpers. lib/index.js is a CommonJS barrel that re-exports the same module unchanged.
tour.languageLesson: A Node.js native addon is a compiled .node file that require() loads like a JavaScript module. node-pre-gyp computes the platform-specific path of that file from the binary block in package.json, so a thin JavaScript wrapper can require it and add helpers on top.

tour.title: Native Binding Core
tour.description: Below lib/mapnik.js is the upstream node-mapnik C++ code in src/. node_mapnik.cpp, the file with the largest fan-out in the graph, is the N-API module entry point: it registers the plugin, font, cache, and blend functions, initializes every wrapper class, and exports constants, dependency versions, and a supports map. mapnik_map.hpp declares the Map wrapper with stylesheet loading, rendering, and an atomic in-use flag; Map.fromString parses a Mapnik XML stylesheet given as a string, and Map.render guards the Map with acquire() and release() while it draws into a mapnik.Image with AGG or into a UTF Grid. utils.hpp holds the shared value_converter that turns Mapnik values into JavaScript values.
tour.languageLesson: node-addon-api wraps the C N-API in C++ classes. A Napi::ObjectWrap<T> subclass binds a C++ object to a JavaScript object and registers its methods, and a Napi::AsyncWorker runs heavy work such as stylesheet parsing or rendering on a worker thread, then calls the JavaScript callback on the main thread. That is why many binding methods come in pairs such as render and renderSync.

tour.title: Images, PNG, UTF Grids
tour.description: The two tile formats from Step 3 come from two native classes. mapnik_image.hpp declares mapnik.Image and is the most depended-on file in the graph; mapnik_image.cpp binds its 33 instance methods and 9 static factories, and mapnik_image_encode.cpp implements Image.encode, which serializes the image in a format such as png and gives the bytes to JavaScript as a Buffer. mapnik_grid.cpp implements mapnik.Grid, a hit buffer of feature ids that encodes into UTFGrid JSON with grid, keys, and data members, and js_grid_utils.hpp does the row-by-row UTF-8 encoding and the attribute collection.
tour.languageLesson: A UTFGrid tells a map client which feature lies under each block of pixels. Each character in the grid rows maps through keys to a feature id, and data holds that feature's attributes, so a client can resolve hover and click events without another request. At resolution 4, one character covers a 4x4 pixel block, so a 256-pixel tile becomes 64 rows of 64 characters.

tour.title: Native Build Toolchain
tour.description: The Makefile is the build entry point for the native addon. Its release and debug targets fetch the mason Mapnik SDK through scripts/install_deps.sh, and its release_base and debug_base targets check for mapnik-config and run node-pre-gyp configure build. binding.gyp compiles the src/*.cpp wrappers from Steps 10 and 11 with include paths and libraries from mapnik-config, and it includes the shared C++14 Release and Debug settings from common.gypi. After the build, scripts/postinstall.sh writes lib/binding/mapnik_settings.js with the font, plugin, and data paths that lib/mapnik.js loads at runtime (Step 9).
tour.languageLesson: GYP is the build description format of node-gyp, which turns targets into platform Makefiles or Visual Studio projects. A .gypi file such as common.gypi holds shared target_defaults that other .gyp files include, and GYP can run a shell command at configure time with <!(...) or <!@(...) to splice in its output, a common way to read flags from a tool such as mapnik-config.

tour.title: Container Image
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the repo into one image in a single build stage. It starts from the prebuilt greenstand/tile-server-base:first image, which must supply the Mapnik libraries and the mapnik-config tool, because the Dockerfile itself installs only build-essential, zlib1g-dev, ca-certificates, and Node.js 14.21.3. It then compiles the native binding with make release_base from Step 12 and runs npm start, which launches greenstand/server.js from Step 2. The .dockerignore excludes node_modules, so host dependencies do not enter the image.
tour.languageLesson: A Dockerfile can start FROM a prebuilt base image to move slow, rarely changing setup (here, the Mapnik libraries) out of every build. A .dockerignore file trims the build context, so COPY . ./ does not send excluded paths such as node_modules into the image.

tour.title: Kubernetes Deployment
tour.description: deployment/ holds a kustomize base that puts the tile server into the tile-server namespace, and beta, development, production, and test overlays patch that base. The base Deployment runs the greenstand/treetracker-map-tile-server image with PORT=3000, PG_POOL_SIZE=20, and both zoom thresholds at 6, and it injects DB_URL from the database-connection SealedSecret, whose PLACEHOLDER value each overlay replaces with a real encrypted connection string. The Service forwards port 80 to container port 3000, and the Ambassador Mapping routes the /tiles/ URL prefix to that Service, rewrites it to /, and allows 60000 ms per request so that slow tile renders do not time out at the gateway.
tour.languageLesson: Kustomize composes a base with per-environment overlays: each overlay lists the base as a resource and applies strategic-merge patches, so only the differences (replicas, env values, CORS, secrets) live in the overlay. A Bitnami SealedSecret holds a value that only the in-cluster sealed-secrets controller can decrypt into a normal Secret, so the encrypted manifest can be stored in git.

tour.title: Release and Deploy Pipelines
tour.description: On every push to master or next, build-deploy.yml runs semantic-release with the .releaserc rules, builds the Dockerfile from Step 13, and pushes greenstand/treetracker-map-tile-server to DockerHub with the package.json version as its tag. A second job sets that tag in deployment/base and applies the development overlay from Step 14 to the DigitalOcean cluster. semantic-release also records each release in CHANGELOG.md, whose top part lists the Greenstand releases from 4.6.0 to 4.36.7 above the inherited node-mapnik history. Promotion is manual: deploy-test.yml and deploy-prod.yml take a chosen git tag and apply the test or production overlay.
tour.languageLesson: A GitHub Actions workflow starts from its on: triggers: push to a branch for automatic releases, or workflow_dispatch for a manual run with inputs such as a git tag. semantic-release reads Conventional Commit messages (feat:, fix:) to choose the next version number, and this repo enforces that format with commitlint through a husky commit-msg hook.
